4.101.s: atha śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe caturthaṃ kāśīkhaṇḍam .. 4 ..
4.101.d: अथ श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराणे चतुर्थं काशीखण्डम् .. 4 ..
4.101.m: Now begins the fourth [book], the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa. // 4

4.101.s: atha kāśīkhaṇḍe pūrvārdham .. (4- 1) ..
4.101.d: अथ काशीखण्डे पूर्वार्धम् .. (4- 1) ..
4.101.m: Now begins the first half in the Kāśīkhaṇḍa. // (4-1)

4.101.s: 1 maṅgalācaraṇam, sūtāgre vyāsasya kāśīkhaṇḍakathopakramakaraṇam, nāradasya narmadāmbhasi snātvoṃkāramabhyarcya ca purato vindhyaparvatadarśanam. prasaṃgena vindhyācalavarṇanam, merustvāmavamanyata iti nāradamunervacaḥ śrutvā vidhyasya vardhanena śrīsūryamārgāvarodhavarṇanaṃ ca... 1 1
4.101.d: 1 मङ्गलाचरणम्, सूताग्रे व्यासस्य काशीखण्डकथोपक्रमकरणम्, नारदस्य नर्मदाम्भसि स्नात्वोंकारमभ्यर्च्य च पुरतो विन्ध्यपर्वतदर्शनम्. प्रसंगेन विन्ध्याचलवर्णनम्, मेरुस्त्वामवमन्यत इति नारदमुनेर्वचः श्रुत्वा विध्यस्य वर्धनेन श्रीसूर्यमार्गावरोधवर्णनं च... 1 1
4.101.m: 1. Auspicious invocation; Vyāsa's commencement of the narration of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa before Sūta; Nārada's beholding the Vindhya mountain before him after bathing in the water of the Narmadā and worshipping Oṃkāra; description of the Vindhyācala in this context; and description of the obstruction of the sun's path by the growth of Vindhya upon hearing the sage Nārada's word: "Meru disdains you." ... 1 1

4.101.s: 2 ekato naiśatimirasaṃbaṃdhādanyatra divākaracaṇḍātapāttrailokyonavasthāvarṇanam, devairvidhistavanam, satyaloke bhayābhāvaṃ darśayituṃ satyalokāgantṛpuruṣapuṇyācāravarṇanapūrvakaṃ vidhikṛtadevasāntvanam, brahmaṇo vacanāttrailokyāpannivāraṇāya śrīkṣetrakāśīsthāgastyamunisamīpe gantuṃ śrīkāśīśakāśīdarśanotsukā'maraprayāṇavarṇanam, saṃkṣepataḥ kāśīvarṇanaṃ ca.. 10 1
4.101.d: 2 एकतो नैशतिमिरसंबंधादन्यत्र दिवाकरचण्डातपात्त्रैलोक्योनवस्थावर्णनम्, देवैर्विधिस्तवनम्, सत्यलोके भयाभावं दर्शयितुं सत्यलोकागन्तृपुरुषपुण्याचारवर्णनपूर्वकं विधिकृतदेवसान्त्वनम्, ब्रह्मणो वचनात्त्रैलोक्यापन्निवारणाय श्रीक्षेत्रकाशीस्थागस्त्यमुनिसमीपे गन्तुं श्रीकाशीशकाशीदर्शनोत्सुकाऽमरप्रयाणवर्णनम्, संक्षेपतः काशीवर्णनं च.. 10 1
4.101.m: 2. Description of the disturbance of the three worlds due to the connection with nocturnal darkness on one side and the fierce heat of the sun on the other; praise of the Creator by the gods; the Creator's consolation of the gods, preceded by a description of the virtuous conduct of persons who go to Satyaloka to demonstrate the absence of fear in Satyaloka; description of the departure of the immortals eager to behold Kāśī and the Lord of Kāśī, in order to approach the sage Agastya dwelling in the sacred field of Kāśī to remove the distress of the three worlds upon Brahmā's word; and a brief description of Kāśī. .. 10 1

4.101.s: 3 kāśīkṣetre maṇikarṇikāsnānaviśveśvaradarśanādiyātrāṃ vidhāya surāṇāmagastyamunyāśrama gamanam, surāṇāṃ tadāśrame lopāmudrāmunyagastvarūpadarśanaṃ ca. 15 1 .
4.101.d: 3 काशीक्षेत्रे मणिकर्णिकास्नानविश्वेश्वरदर्शनादियात्रां विधाय सुराणामगस्त्यमुन्याश्रम गमनम्, सुराणां तदाश्रमे लोपामुद्रामुन्यगस्त्वरूपदर्शनं च. 15 1 .
4.101.m: 3. The gods' journey to the hermitage of the sage Agastya after performing the pilgrimage consisting of bathing at Maṇikarṇikā and the darśana of Viśveśvara in the sacred field of Kāśī; and the gods' beholding the forms of Lopāmudrā and the sage Agastya in his hermitage. 15 1 .

4.101.s: 4 bṛhaspatipraṇītāgasyamunistutiprasaṃgena lopāmudrāvarṇanam, etatprasaṅgena pativratācāranirūpaṇam, sūryamārganirodhakavindhyavṛddhinivāraṇāya prārthayamānasya surācāryasya vacanānusāreṇāgastyenāmarāśvāsanam, amarāṇāṃ svargalokagamanaṃ ca. 20 1
4.101.d: 4 बृहस्पतिप्रणीतागस्यमुनिस्तुतिप्रसंगेन लोपामुद्रावर्णनम्, एतत्प्रसङ्गेन पतिव्रताचारनिरूपणम्, सूर्यमार्गनिरोधकविन्ध्यवृद्धिनिवारणाय प्रार्थयमानस्य सुराचार्यस्य वचनानुसारेणागस्त्येनामराश्वासनम्, अमराणां स्वर्गलोकगमनं च. 20 1
4.101.m: 4. Description of Lopāmudrā in the context of the eulogy of the sage Agastya composed by Bṛhaspati; exposition of the duties of a devoted wife in this context; Agastya's consoling of the immortals according to the request of the teacher of the gods who prayed for the cessation of the growth of Vindhya obstructing the sun's path; and the departure of the immortals to the heavenly world. 20 1

4.101.s: 5 amaraprārthanāmaṅgīkṛtya vindhyavṛddhinirākaraṇāya bhāryayā sahā'gastyamuneḥ kāśīkṣetrādbahiḥ prayāṇam, kāśīviyogaduḥkhitasya munerviśvanāthakālabhairavādidevatājñāgrahaṇapūrvakaṃ viśeṣato vilāpakaraṇam, agastyamunimāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā vindhyasya kharvatāsvīkāraḥ, yāvanmamāgamanaṃ punarna bhavettāvatkharvataro bhaveti muneradriṃ prati kathanam, munermahālakṣmīdarśanam, agastyamunināḥ mahālakṣmīstotrakaraṇam, mahālakṣmyā'gastyāya varapradānam, agastasyāgre prayāṇaṃ ca..... ... 23
4.101.d: 5 अमरप्रार्थनामङ्गीकृत्य विन्ध्यवृद्धिनिराकरणाय भार्यया सहाऽगस्त्यमुनेः काशीक्षेत्राद्बहिः प्रयाणम्, काशीवियोगदुःखितस्य मुनेर्विश्वनाथकालभैरवादिदेवताज्ञाग्रहणपूर्वकं विशेषतो विलापकरणम्, अगस्त्यमुनिमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा विन्ध्यस्य खर्वतास्वीकारः, यावन्ममागमनं पुनर्न भवेत्तावत्खर्वतरो भवेति मुनेरद्रिं प्रति कथनम्, मुनेर्महालक्ष्मीदर्शनम्, अगस्त्यमुनिनाः महालक्ष्मीस्तोत्रकरणम्, महालक्ष्म्याऽगस्त्याय वरप्रदानम्, अगस्तस्याग्रे प्रयाणं च..... ... 23
4.101.m: 5. The departure of the sage Agastya outside the sacred field of Kāśī with his wife to stop the growth of Vindhya, having accepted the prayer of the immortals; the sage's extensive lamentation, afflicted by the grief of separation from Kāśī, having first taken leave of deities such as Viśvanātha and Kālabhairava; Vindhya's assumption of a dwarfed form upon seeing the sage Agastya approach; the sage's statement to the mountain: "Remain even more dwarfed until my return"; the sage's darśana of Mahālakṣmī; the composition of the Mahālakṣmī hymn by the sage Agastya; Mahālakṣmī's granting of a boon to Agastya; and Agastya's further departure. 23

4.101.s: 6 paropakārapraśaṃsanam, śrīśailaśikharādipuṇyasthānadarśanena muktiścetkiṃ kāśīmahattvamiti lopāmudrāpraśnaḥ, tīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaprasaṅgena kāśīkṣetramahattvakathanam, sarvatīrthāni kāśīkṣetraprāpakāṇīti kāśīśraiṣṭhyadyotanaṃ ca.. .. ... 30 2
4.101.d: 6 परोपकारप्रशंसनम्, श्रीशैलशिखरादिपुण्यस्थानदर्शनेन मुक्तिश्चेत्किं काशीमहत्त्वमिति लोपामुद्राप्रश्नः, तीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनप्रसङ्गेन काशीक्षेत्रमहत्त्वकथनम्, सर्वतीर्थानि काशीक्षेत्रप्रापकाणीति काशीश्रैष्ठ्यद्योतनं च.. .. ... 30 2
4.101.m: 6. Praise of helping others; Lopāmudrā's question: "If liberation comes from the sight of holy places like the summit of Śrīśaila, what is the greatness of Kāśī?"; the account of the greatness of the sacred field of Kāśī in the context of describing the māhātmya of sacred fords; and highlighting the supremacy of Kāśī with the principle that all sacred fords lead to the sacred field of Kāśī. .. 30 2

4.101.s:
7 śivaśarmākhyasya mathurāpurīsthadvijasya svadehe samāgatāṃ jarāṃ dṛṣṭvā cintodgārāḥ, saptapurīyātrārthaṃ gṛhādbahirdvijasya prayāṇam, ayodhyāyātrāṃ samāpya prayāge samāgamanam, prasaṅgena prayāgamāhātmyavarṇanam, dvijasya kāśīyātrākathanam, tasya mahākālapurīprayāṇam, tatprasaṅgānmahākālamāhātmyakathanam, māyāpurītīrthayātrākathanam, dvijasya māyāpuryāṃ dehāvasānam, puṇyaśīlasuśīlanāmakavaiṣṇavagaṇā-
dhiṣṭhitasvarṇavimānamāsthāya dvijasya nabhovartmārohaṇaṃ ca.. 33 1
4.101.d:
7 शिवशर्माख्यस्य मथुरापुरीस्थद्विजस्य स्वदेहे समागतां जरां दृष्ट्वा चिन्तोद्गाराः, सप्तपुरीयात्रार्थं गृहाद्बहिर्द्विजस्य प्रयाणम्, अयोध्यायात्रां समाप्य प्रयागे समागमनम्, प्रसङ्गेन प्रयागमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, द्विजस्य काशीयात्राकथनम्, तस्य महाकालपुरीप्रयाणम्, तत्प्रसङ्गान्महाकालमाहात्म्यकथनम्, मायापुरीतीर्थयात्राकथनम्, द्विजस्य मायापुर्यां देहावसानम्, पुण्यशीलसुशीलनामकवैष्णवगणा-
धिष्ठितस्वर्णविमानमास्थाय द्विजस्य नभोवर्त्मारोहणं च.. 33 1
4.101.m: 7. The reflections of concern of a brahmin named Śivaśarman residing in the city of Mathurā upon seeing old age come upon his body; the brahmin's departure from his home to undertake a pilgrimage to the seven sacred cities; his arrival at Prayāga after completing the pilgrimage to Ayodhyā; description of the Prayāgamāhātmya in this context; account of the brahmin's pilgrimage to Kāśī; his departure to the city of Mahākāla; account of the Mahākālamāhātmya in that context; account of the pilgrimage to the sacred ford of Māyāpurī; the end of the brahmin's body in Māyāpurī; and the brahmin's ascent to the path of the sky, having mounted a golden aerial chariot occupied by the Vaiṣṇava attendants named Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla. .. 33 1

4.101.s:
8 māyākhyāyāṃ muktipuryāṃ mṛtasya śivaśamarṇo dvijasya kathaṃ mokṣānavāptiriti lopāmudrāsatīpraśnaḥ, māyādiṣu ṣaṭpurīṣu sākṣātsāyujyaṃ nāstīti darśayituṃ śivaśarmaviṣṇugaṇasaṃvādārambhaḥ, dvijapraśnānusāreṇa piśācaguhyakagandharvalokasthitapuruṣasaṃpāditasadācāravarṇanam, yamalokamāgatasya dvijasya śivaśarmaṇaḥ satkārapūrvakapūjanārthaṃ dharmarājasyāgamanam, dharmarājasya saumyamūrteḥ saumyavacāṃsi śrutvā
kathamidamiti dvijapraśnaḥ, yamasya rūpadvayanirūpaṇaprasaṅgena saṃkṣepato yamalokavarṇanaṃ ca ..... 38
4.101.d:
8 मायाख्यायां मुक्तिपुर्यां मृतस्य शिवशमर्णो द्विजस्य कथं मोक्षानवाप्तिरिति लोपामुद्रासतीप्रश्नः, मायादिषु षट्पुरीषु साक्षात्सायुज्यं नास्तीति दर्शयितुं शिवशर्मविष्णुगणसंवादारम्भः, द्विजप्रश्नानुसारेण पिशाचगुह्यकगन्धर्वलोकस्थितपुरुषसंपादितसदाचारवर्णनम्, यमलोकमागतस्य द्विजस्य शिवशर्मणः सत्कारपूर्वकपूजनार्थं धर्मराजस्यागमनम्, धर्मराजस्य सौम्यमूर्तेः सौम्यवचांसि श्रुत्वा
कथमिदमिति द्विजप्रश्नः, यमस्य रूपद्वयनिरूपणप्रसङ्गेन संक्षेपतो यमलोकवर्णनं च ..... 38
4.101.m: 8 The virtuous Lopāmudrā's question: how did the brahmin Śivaśarman, having died in the liberation-city called Māyā, not attain liberation? The beginning of the dialogue between Śivaśarman and the attendants of Viṣṇu to show that direct union [with God] does not occur in the six cities beginning with Māyā; according to the brahmin's question, a description of the virtuous conduct achieved by men dwelling in the worlds of Piśācas, Guhyakas, and Gandharvas; the arrival of Dharmarāja to worship the brahmin Śivaśarman, who had arrived in the world of Yama, with hospitality; the brahmin's question, 'How is this?', upon hearing the gentle words of Dharmarāja of gentle form; and a concise description of the world of Yama in the context of delineating Yama's two forms: 38.

4.101.s: 9 apsarolokavarṇanam, sūryalokavarṇanam, sūryopāsanāvarṇanaprasaṅgena gāyatrīmantramāhātmyanirūpaṇam, arghapradānavidhinirūpaṇaṃ ca.. 43 1
4.101.d: 9 अप्सरोलोकवर्णनम्, सूर्यलोकवर्णनम्, सूर्योपासनावर्णनप्रसङ्गेन गायत्रीमन्त्रमाहात्म्यनिरूपणम्, अर्घप्रदानविधिनिरूपणं च.. 43 1
4.101.m: 9 Description of the world of the apsarases; description of the world of Sūrya; delineation of the greatness of the Gāyatrī mantra in the context of describing the worship of Sūrya; and delineation of the procedure for offering argha: 43 1.

4.101.s: 10 sahasrākṣapuravarṇanam, arciṣmatyākhyavītihotrapurīvarṇanam, kṛśānūtpattikathanaprasaṃgena jyotiṣmatīpurīsthaviśvānarākhyamunītihāsakathanam, śuciṣmatīkathanānusāreṇa muneḥ kāśīkṣetre gatvā vīreśvaraśivaliṅgasamīpe tapo'nuṣṭhānakathanam, trayodaśe māsibālarūpeṇa liṅge śivadarśanam, abhilāṣāṣṭakastotrakathanam, śivādvaralābhena santuṣṭasya muneḥ svagṛhe prayāṇaṃ ca.. - .... ... 46
4.101.d: 10 सहस्राक्षपुरवर्णनम्, अर्चिष्मत्याख्यवीतिहोत्रपुरीवर्णनम्, कृशानूत्पत्तिकथनप्रसंगेन ज्योतिष्मतीपुरीस्थविश्वानराख्यमुनीतिहासकथनम्, शुचिष्मतीकथनानुसारेण मुनेः काशीक्षेत्रे गत्वा वीरेश्वरशिवलिङ्गसमीपे तपोऽनुष्ठानकथनम्, त्रयोदशे मासिबालरूपेण लिङ्गे शिवदर्शनम्, अभिलाषाष्टकस्तोत्रकथनम्, शिवाद्वरलाभेन सन्तुष्टस्य मुनेः स्वगृहे प्रयाणं च.. - .... ... 46
4.101.m: 10 Description of the city of Sahasrākṣa [Indra]; description of the city of Vītihotra [Agni] named Arciṣmatī; narration of the story of the sage named Viśvānara residing in the city of Jyotiṣmatī in the context of narrating the origin of Kṛśānu [Fire]; narration of the sage's performance of austerity near the Vīreśvara-śivaliṅga after going to the sacred field of Kāśī according to Śuciṣmatī's words; darśana of Śiva in child form in the liṅga in the thirteenth month; recital of the hymn Abhilāṣāṣṭaka; and the departure of the sage, satisfied by receiving a boon from Śiva, to his own home: 46.

4.101.s: 11 kālāntareṇa viśvānarācchuciṣmatyāṃ garbhādhānam, śubhamuhūrte sutotpattiḥ, jātakarmādasaṃskāranirūpaṇam, hastasāmudrikaṃ vīkṣya nāradoktaṃ vaiśvānarākhyasya bālasya gaṇḍāntaṃ śrutvā mātāpitrāḥ śokakaraṇam , apamṛtyuharaṇāya munikumārasya kāśyāṃ liṅga saṃsthāpyānuṣṭhānakaraṇam, tṛtīyasaṃvatsare varapradānāya samāgatasya kuliśāyudhasya munikumāraṃ pratiṃ vacanam, 'nāhaṃ tvatto varāngrahītumutsahe' iti vacaḥ śrutvā indrasya kuliśapātanodyogaṃ vilokya munikumārasya mūrcchāvagamaḥ, tatraiva śiva-prādurbhāvaḥ, śivavarādvaiśvānarasya dikpatitvādiprāptivarṇanaṃ ca.. ... .. 51
4.101.d: 11 कालान्तरेण विश्वानराच्छुचिष्मत्यां गर्भाधानम्, शुभमुहूर्ते सुतोत्पत्तिः, जातकर्मादसंस्कारनिरूपणम्, हस्तसामुद्रिकं वीक्ष्य नारदोक्तं वैश्वानराख्यस्य बालस्य गण्डान्तं श्रुत्वा मातापित्राः शोककरणम् , अपमृत्युहरणाय मुनिकुमारस्य काश्यां लिङ्ग संस्थाप्यानुष्ठानकरणम्, तृतीयसंवत्सरे वरप्रदानाय समागतस्य कुलिशायुधस्य मुनिकुमारं प्रतिं वचनम्, ऽनाहं त्वत्तो वरान्ग्रहीतुमुत्सहे' इति वचः श्रुत्वा इन्द्रस्य कुलिशपातनोद्योगं विलोक्य मुनिकुमारस्य मूर्च्छावगमः, तत्रैव शिव-प्रादुर्भावः, शिववराद्वैश्वानरस्य दिक्पतित्वादिप्राप्तिवर्णनं च.. ... .. 51
4.101.m: 11 In course of time, impregnation of Śuciṣmatī by Viśvānara; birth of a son at an auspicious moment; delineation of the birth-rites and other consecrations; grief of the parents upon hearing from Nārada the inauspicious astrological junction (gaṇḍānta) of the boy named Vaiśvānara after examining the palmistry; the sage's son installing a liṅga in Kāśī and performing spiritual practice to avert premature death; the speech to the sage's son by the thunderbolt-armed [Indra] who arrived in the third year to grant a boon; the sage's son fainting upon seeing Indra preparing to strike with his thunderbolt after hearing his words, 'I do not wish to accept a boon from you'; the appearance of Śiva right there; and description of Vaiśvānara's attainment of guardianship of a quarter and other [offices] through Śiva's boon: 51.

4.101.s: 12 nairṛtalokavaṇarnam, vindhyāṭavyāṃ pallīpateḥ piṃgākṣasya viśvanāthapurīṃ pratiṃ yātukāmasya sārthasya prāṇaparirakṣaṇārthaṃ prāṇadānāllokapālatvaprāptiḥ, vāruṇalokavarṇanam, kardamasya prajāpateḥ putrasya śuciṣmato jalakrīḍāyāṃ śiśumāreṇa sarasyāharaṇam, sarasi magnaṃ śrutvā'pi sutaṃ pūjāyāmadhikāsaktasya muneḥ savidhe śivagaṇena saśiśumārasya bālakasyānayanam, śuciṣmato munikumārasya kāśyāṃ śivaliṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya tapaścaraṇam, śivaprasādādvāruṇalokasaṃprāptiśca.. .... 57
4.101.d: 12 नैरृतलोकवणर्नम्, विन्ध्याटव्यां पल्लीपतेः पिंगाक्षस्य विश्वनाथपुरीं प्रतिं यातुकामस्य सार्थस्य प्राणपरिरक्षणार्थं प्राणदानाल्लोकपालत्वप्राप्तिः, वारुणलोकवर्णनम्, कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः पुत्रस्य शुचिष्मतो जलक्रीडायां शिशुमारेण सरस्याहरणम्, सरसि मग्नं श्रुत्वाऽपि सुतं पूजायामधिकासक्तस्य मुनेः सविधे शिवगणेन सशिशुमारस्य बालकस्यानयनम्, शुचिष्मतो मुनिकुमारस्य काश्यां शिवलिंगं संस्थाप्य तपश्चरणम्, शिवप्रसादाद्वारुणलोकसंप्राप्तिश्च.. .... 57
4.101.m: 12 Description of the world of Nirṛti; Piṅgākṣa, chieftain of an outpost in the Vindhya forest, obtaining the status of a world-guardian through the sacrifice of his life to protect the lives of a caravan wishing to go to the city of Viśvanātha; description of the world of Varuṇa; Śuciṣmat, son of the Prajāpati Kardama, being seized by an alligator in a lake during water-sports; the bringing of the boy along with the alligator to the presence of the sage who, even upon hearing his son was submerged in the lake, remained deeply engaged in worship, by the attendant of Śiva; the sage's son Śuciṣmat installing a śivaliṅga in Kāśī and practicing austerity; and the attainment of the world of Varuṇa through Śiva's grace: 57.

4.101.s:
13 jagatprāṇasya pavanasya gaṃdhavatīpurīvarṇanam, kaśyapaputrasya pūtātmanaḥ śrīkāśīkṣetre liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya tapaścaraṇam, tasya śivāllokapālatvaprāptikathanam, guhyakeśvarasyālakāvatīpurīvarṇanam, kāmpilyanagare yajñadattanāmno brāhmaṇasya nāmnā guṇaṃnidhirapyaguṇanidhirdyutāsakto madyapaḥ putro babhūva tasya mātrā bahukālaṃ pracchannadurācārasya sutasya duṣkṛtiṃ saṃpaśyatā pitrā svagṛhānniṣkāsanam, svārthaṃ dīpadaśodyotena liṃgamaulitamoharasya bahūpoṣitasyāsya śivarātryāṃ śivālaye 'nnāpaharaṇādghātitasya kaliṅgadeśarājaputratvaprāptivarṇanam, tatra tasya śivālayeṣu dīpadānātkalpāntare viśravaḥsutatvamabhigabhya duḥsahatapaścaraṇataḥ śivasakhyālakārājyādilā-
bhavarṇanaṃ ca-. .. .. ... .. .. 61
4.101.d:
13 जगत्प्राणस्य पवनस्य गंधवतीपुरीवर्णनम्, कश्यपपुत्रस्य पूतात्मनः श्रीकाशीक्षेत्रे लिंगं संस्थाप्य तपश्चरणम्, तस्य शिवाल्लोकपालत्वप्राप्तिकथनम्, गुह्यकेश्वरस्यालकावतीपुरीवर्णनम्, काम्पिल्यनगरे यज्ञदत्तनाम्नो ब्राह्मणस्य नाम्ना गुणंनिधिरप्यगुणनिधिर्द्युतासक्तो मद्यपः पुत्रो बभूव तस्य मात्रा बहुकालं प्रच्छन्नदुराचारस्य सुतस्य दुष्कृतिं संपश्यता पित्रा स्वगृहान्निष्कासनम्, स्वार्थं दीपदशोद्योतेन लिंगमौलितमोहरस्य बहूपोषितस्यास्य शिवरात्र्यां शिवालये ऽन्नापहरणाद्घातितस्य कलिङ्गदेशराजपुत्रत्वप्राप्तिवर्णनम्, तत्र तस्य शिवालयेषु दीपदानात्कल्पान्तरे विश्रवःसुतत्वमभिगभ्य दुःसहतपश्चरणतः शिवसख्यालकाराज्यादिला-
भवर्णनं च-. .. .. ... .. .. 61
4.101.m: 13 Description of Gandhavatī, the city of Pavana [Wind], the life-breath of the world; the pure-souled son of Kaśyapa installing a liṅga in the sacred field of Kāśī and practicing austerity; narration of his attainment of the status of a world-guardian from Śiva; description of Alakāvatī, the city of the lord of Guhyakas [Kubera]; in the city of Kāmpilya, a brahmin named Yajñadatta had a son named Guṇanidhi, who, though named Guṇanidhi ('treasury of virtues'), was a treasury of vices, addicted to gambling and a drinker of liquor; his expulsion from his own house by his father who noticed the misdeeds of his son, whose wicked conduct had long been concealed by his mother; description of his obtaining the state of a prince of Kaliṅga after being killed for stealing food in a Śiva temple on Śivarātri, having fasted for many [days] and having removed the darkness over the top of the liṅga for his own purpose by brightening the wick of a lamp; and description of his attaining the status of the son of Viśravas in another kalpa, and obtaining the friendship of Śiva, kingship over Alakā, and other [rewards] through the performance of unbearable austerity, owing to the donation of lamps in Śiva temples there: 61.

4.101.s: 14 rudrabhaktoṣitaiśānīpurīvarṇanam ,ajaikapādādirudragaṇasthāpitaiśānaliègamāhātmyavarṇanam, candralokavarṇanam, brahmaṇo mānasātsamudbhūtasya somasya vārāṇasyāṃ liṃgaṃ vidhāya tatpuro mahattapaścaraṇam, śivaprasādāttasya mahaiśvaryalābhakathanaṃ ca. 66 2
4.101.d: 14 रुद्रभक्तोषितैशानीपुरीवर्णनम् ,अजैकपादादिरुद्रगणस्थापितैशानलिèगमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, चन्द्रलोकवर्णनम्, ब्रह्मणो मानसात्समुद्भूतस्य सोमस्य वाराणस्यां लिंगं विधाय तत्पुरो महत्तपश्चरणम्, शिवप्रसादात्तस्य महैश्वर्यलाभकथनं च. 66 2
4.101.m: 14 Description of the city of Aiśānī inhabited by devotees of Rudra; description of the greatness of the Aiśāna-liṅga established by the Rudra hosts such as Ajaikapād; description of the world of Candra; Soma, who arose from the mind of Brahmā, setting up a liṅga in Vārāṇasī and performing great austerity before it; and narration of his attainment of great sovereignty through Śiva's grace: 66 2.

4.101.s: 15 dakṣaprajāpateḥ ṣaṣṭiduhitṛmadhye rohiṇyādibhiḥ saptaviṃśatibhiḥ kanyābhirekapatilābhāya liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya vārāṇasyāṃ tapaḥkaraṇācchivavarānusārataḥ somaṃ patimāsādya saṃpāditasya nakṣatralokasya saṃkṣepato varṇanam, atriputrasya somasya gurubhāryāpaharaṇam, rudracandramasoryuddhakathanam, yuddhaṃ nivārya brahmaṇo vacanāccandrasya bṛhaspataye tārāsamarpaṇam, tasyāṃ budhasyotpattiḥ, budhakṛtaśivārādhanam, budhasya śivavarāllokapālatvādivaraiśvaryalābhavarṇanaṃ ca. ........ 68 2
4.101.d: 15 दक्षप्रजापतेः षष्टिदुहितृमध्ये रोहिण्यादिभिः सप्तविंशतिभिः कन्याभिरेकपतिलाभाय लिंगं संस्थाप्य वाराणस्यां तपःकरणाच्छिववरानुसारतः सोमं पतिमासाद्य संपादितस्य नक्षत्रलोकस्य संक्षेपतो वर्णनम्, अत्रिपुत्रस्य सोमस्य गुरुभार्यापहरणम्, रुद्रचन्द्रमसोर्युद्धकथनम्, युद्धं निवार्य ब्रह्मणो वचनाच्चन्द्रस्य बृहस्पतये तारासमर्पणम्, तस्यां बुधस्योत्पत्तिः, बुधकृतशिवाराधनम्, बुधस्य शिववराल्लोकपालत्वादिवरैश्वर्यलाभवर्णनं च. ........ 68 2
4.101.m: 15 Brief description of the world of the constellations achieved by obtaining Soma as their husband in accordance with Śiva's boon, after twenty-seven maidens among the sixty daughters of Dakṣa Prajāpati, beginning with Rohiṇī, installed a liṅga and performed austerity in Vārāṇasī in order to obtain a single husband; Soma, son of Atri, abducting the guru's wife; narration of the battle between Rudra and Candramas; Candra handing over Tārā to Bṛhaspati at the word of Brahmā after the battle was averted; the birth of Budha in her; the worship of Śiva performed by Budha; and description of Budha's attainment of boons and sovereignty such as the status of a world-guardian through the boon of Śiva: 68 2.

4.101.s: 16 samare devairghātitānāṃ dānavendrāndhakasainikānāṃ saṃjīvanīmantrato bhārgavaśukreṇa punarujjīvanam, devaprārthanayā śivena naṃdikeśvaradvārā śukramānāyya svamukhe tasya nikṣepaṇam, andhakasya sasainyasya pramathaiḥ saha yuddhavarṇanam, śukrataḥ śukrasya bahirniḥsaraṇam, śukrasya vārāṇasyāṃ tapaścaraṇācchivaprasādato lokādhipatyādivaraprāptivarṇanaṃ ca.. ...... ..... ... 71 2
4.101.d: 16 समरे देवैर्घातितानां दानवेन्द्रान्धकसैनिकानां संजीवनीमन्त्रतो भार्गवशुक्रेण पुनरुज्जीवनम्, देवप्रार्थनया शिवेन नंदिकेश्वरद्वारा शुक्रमानाय्य स्वमुखे तस्य निक्षेपणम्, अन्धकस्य ससैन्यस्य प्रमथैः सह युद्धवर्णनम्, शुक्रतः शुक्रस्य बहिर्निःसरणम्, शुक्रस्य वाराणस्यां तपश्चरणाच्छिवप्रसादतो लोकाधिपत्यादिवरप्राप्तिवर्णनं च.. ...... ..... ... 71 2
4.101.m: 16 The revival through the Saṃjīvanī mantra, by Śukra the descendant of Bhṛgu, of the soldiers of Andhaka, lord of the Dānavas, slain in battle by the gods; Śiva, at the prayer of the gods, having Śukra brought through Nandikeśvara and throwing him into his mouth; description of the battle of Andhaka along with his army against the Pramathas; the emergence of Śukra from semen; and description of Śukra's attainment of boons such as lordship over a world through the grace of Śiva by performing austerity in Vārāṇasī: 71 2.

4.101.s: 17 śrīśivasya bhālasthalato bhūmau nipatitātsvedabindorlohitāṅgasyotpattiḥ, śivaprasādāttasya lokādhipatyādikathanam, aṅgirasasya śivaprasādārthaṃ vārāṇasyāṃ tapaḥkaraṇam, śivasya varaprasādāllokapatitvadevagurutvalābhaḥ, mārtaṇḍātsaṃjñāpratikṛtau chāyāyāṃ śanaiścarotpattikathanam, tasya vārāṇasyāṃ tapaścaraṇāllokapālatvagrahamukhyatvalābhavarṇanaṃ ca................. 76 2
4.101.d: 17 श्रीशिवस्य भालस्थलतो भूमौ निपतितात्स्वेदबिन्दोर्लोहिताङ्गस्योत्पत्तिः, शिवप्रसादात्तस्य लोकाधिपत्यादिकथनम्, अङ्गिरसस्य शिवप्रसादार्थं वाराणस्यां तपःकरणम्, शिवस्य वरप्रसादाल्लोकपतित्वदेवगुरुत्वलाभः, मार्तण्डात्संज्ञाप्रतिकृतौ छायायां शनैश्चरोत्पत्तिकथनम्, तस्य वाराणस्यां तपश्चरणाल्लोकपालत्वग्रहमुख्यत्वलाभवर्णनं च................. 76 2
4.101.m: 17 The birth of Lohitāṅga [Mars] from a drop of sweat that fell to the earth from the forehead of the glorious Śiva; narration of his lordship over a world and other [rewards] through Śiva's grace; Aṅgiras performing austerity in Vārāṇasī for the grace of Śiva; [his] attainment of the status of a world-guardian and the guru of the gods through the grace of Śiva's boon; narration of the birth of Śanaiścara from Mārtaṇḍa in Chāyā, the likeness of Saṃjñā; and description of his attainment of the status of a world-guardian and chief among the planets through performing austerity in Vārāṇasī: 76 2.

4.101.s: 18 brahmamānasasṛṣṭamarīcyādiputrasaptarṣilokavarṇanam, arundhatīnakṣatrasthānadarśanādivarṇanaṃ ca. .... ..... ... ... .... 81 1
4.101.d: 18 ब्रह्ममानससृष्टमरीच्यादिपुत्रसप्तर्षिलोकवर्णनम्, अरुन्धतीनक्षत्रस्थानदर्शनादिवर्णनं च. .... ..... ... ... .... 81 1
4.101.m: 18 Description of the world of the seven seers, the sons born of the mind of Brahmā beginning with Marīci; and description of seeing the place of the star Arundhatī and other matters: 81 1.

4.101.s: 19 pituraṃkādhiṣṭhitasya sāpatnamātrā tiraskṛtasya dhruvasya mātṛvacanāttapasyārthaṃ vipinapraveśaḥ, tatra saptarṣisamāgamaḥ, tasmai dvādśākṣaramantramupadiśya munīnāmantardhānaṃ ca. 82 1
4.101.d: 19 पितुरंकाधिष्ठितस्य सापत्नमात्रा तिरस्कृतस्य ध्रुवस्य मातृवचनात्तपस्यार्थं विपिनप्रवेशः, तत्र सप्तर्षिसमागमः, तस्मै द्वाद्शाक्षरमन्त्रमुपदिश्य मुनीनामन्तर्धानं च. 82 1
4.101.m: 19. Dhruva, seated on his father’s lap, is rebuked by his stepmother; at his mother's word he enters the forest to perform tapas; there he meets the Seven Seers; the munis instruct him in the twelve-syllable mantra and disappear. 82 1

4.101.s: 20 yamunātaṭe madhuvane sthitasya dhruvasya tapasyāvarṇanam, indrapreṣitanānāvidhatapovighna nirūpaṇam, dhruvasya sākṣācchrībhagavato darśanaṃ ca ... ... ( 86 2
4.101.d: 20 यमुनातटे मधुवने स्थितस्य ध्रुवस्य तपस्यावर्णनम्, इन्द्रप्रेषितनानाविधतपोविघ्न निरूपणम्, ध्रुवस्य साक्षाच्छ्रीभगवतो दर्शनं च ... ... ( 86 2
4.101.m: 20. Description of the tapas of Dhruva staying in Madhuvana on the bank of the Yamunā; description of the various obstacles to tapas sent by Indra; and Dhruva’s direct vision of the Lord. 86 2

4.101.s: 21 dhruvakṛtaśrībhagavatstotranirūpaṇam, jyotiścakrasyādhārapadaṃ te dāsyāmi tathāpi mayā saha kāśī yāhi tatra liṃgārcanaṃ kṛtvā kṛtakṛtyo bhava iti dhruvaṃ sandiśya tena saha bhagavataḥ kāśīpuryāṃ prayāṇam, tatra dhruvasya liṃgasthāpanena kṛtakṛtyatvamāsādya svagṛhe prayāṇaṃ ca. - -.. 90 1
4.101.d: 21 ध्रुवकृतश्रीभगवत्स्तोत्रनिरूपणम्, ज्योतिश्चक्रस्याधारपदं ते दास्यामि तथापि मया सह काशी याहि तत्र लिंगार्चनं कृत्वा कृतकृत्यो भव इति ध्रुवं सन्दिश्य तेन सह भगवतः काशीपुर्यां प्रयाणम्, तत्र ध्रुवस्य लिंगस्थापनेन कृतकृत्यत्वमासाद्य स्वगृहे प्रयाणं च. - -.. 90 1
4.101.m: 21. Description of the hymn of praise to the Lord composed by Dhruva; the Lord instructs Dhruva: “I shall give you the foundational position of the wheel of luminaries; even so, go with me to Kāśī; having worshipped the liṅga there, achieve your purpose”; the Lord departs with him to the city of Kāśī; there Dhruva achieves his purpose by establishing a liṅga, and returns home. 90 1

4.101.m: 24. A brahmin, dying in Māyāpurī, attains various kinds of enjoyment in the world of Viṣṇu for a year of Brahmā; then, upon the exhaustion of his merit, he becomes a king in the village of Nandivardhana and pleases his subjects; experiencing joy upon hearing the Kāśīmāhātmya, he departs for Kāśī; by the grace of Viśveśvara he builds a temple to Śiva there; description of the future condition of the brahmin Śivaśarman, as declared by the attendants of Viṣṇu, [namely] that after an examination by Śiva, who had come to test him as he performed tapas before the installed Śivaliṅga named Vṛddhakāleśvara, the king along with his wife would merge into that very liṅga together with him. 101 1

4.101.m: 28. Description of the pacification of mortal sins and secondary sins through bathing in the Gaṅgā at Kāśī by virtue of Śiva’s presence; a certain nominal brahmin named Vāhīka, the husband of a Śūdra woman, is killed in a forest in Kaliṅga by a tiger; a vulture takes his flesh along with the bone and, while flying, fights with another vulture; by divine destiny the bone falls into the water of the Gaṅgā; the great wonder resulting from contact with the water of the Gaṅgā; astonishment of all upon seeing that this Vāhīka, though cast into hells such as Kumbhīpāka for the purification of various sins, experiences pleasure; at last, mounting a vimāna, Vāhīka departs for the heavenly realm; and exposition of the Gaṅgāmāhātmya. 119 1

4.101.s: 48 kṛṣṇaputrasya sāṃbasya nāradāpamānātkṛṣṇaśāpaprabhavakuṣṭharogāvagamakathanam, tatparihārāya kāśyāṃ tasya svanāmnā kuṇḍaṃ vidhāya tapaścaraṇādroganivṛttiḥ, kuṇḍamāhātmyasahitasāṃbādityamāhātmyakathanaṃ ca. ...... .... ... 215 1

4.101.m: 49. In the context of the Pāṇḍavas' forest exile, their journey to Kāśī; there Draupadī's worship of the Sun, her receiving the pot from the Sun, identification of the place of the Sun worshipped by Draupadī, and description of the māhātmya of Mayūkhāditya. 217 1

5.1.s:
oṃnamaḥ puruṣottamāya..
..atha skānde mahāpurāṇe ṣaṣṭhanāgarakhaṇḍaprārambhaḥ..
..vyāsa uvāca..
sa dhūrjaṭi jaṭājūṭo jāyatāṃ vijayāya vaḥ.
yatraikapalitabhrāṃtiṃ karotyadyāpi jāhnavī..6.1.1..
5.1.d:
ओंनमः पुरुषोत्तमाय..
..अथ स्कान्दे महापुराणे षष्ठनागरखण्डप्रारम्भः..
..व्यास उवाच..
स धूर्जटि जटाजूटो जायतां विजयाय वः.
यत्रैकपलितभ्रांतिं करोत्यद्यापि जाह्नवी..6.1.1..
5.1.m:
Om, homage to Puruṣottama.
Now begins the sixth [section], the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa.
Vyāsa said:
May the matted hair of Dhūrjaṭi lead to your victory,
wherein the Jāhnavī even today causes the illusion of a single grey strand.

5.1.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ.
harasya pūjyate liṃgaṃ kasmādatanmahāmate
viśeṣātsaṃparityajya śeṣāṃgāni surāsuraiḥ..6.1.2..
5.1.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः.
हरस्य पूज्यते लिंगं कस्मादतन्महामते
विशेषात्संपरित्यज्य शेषांगानि सुरासुरैः..6.1.2..
5.1.m:
The seers said:
Why, O high-minded one, is the liṅga of Hara worshipped
specifically by gods and demons, leaving aside the rest of his limbs?

5.1.s:
tasmādetanmahābāho yathāvadvaktumarhasi.
sāṃprataṃ sūta kārtsnyena paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ..6.1.3..
5.1.d:
तस्मादेतन्महाबाहो यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि.
सांप्रतं सूत कार्त्स्न्येन परं कौतूहलं हि नः..6.1.3..
5.1.m:
Therefore, O mighty-armed one, you ought to tell this properly
in full now, O Sūta, for our curiosity is indeed great.

5.1.s:
sūta uvāca.
praśnabhāro mahāneṣa yo bhavadbhirudāhṛtaḥ.
kīrtayiṣye tathāpyenaṃ namaskṛtya svayaṃbhuve..6.1.4..
5.1.d:
सूत उवाच.
प्रश्नभारो महानेष यो भवद्भिरुदाहृतः.
कीर्तयिष्ये तथाप्येनं नमस्कृत्य स्वयंभुवे..6.1.4..

5.1.s:
ānartaviṣaye cāsti vanaṃ munijanāśrayam.
manojñaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvartuphalitadrumam..6.1.5..
5.1.d:
आनर्तविषये चास्ति वनं मुनिजनाश्रयम्.
मनोज्ञं सर्वसत्त्वानां सर्वर्तुफलितद्रुमम्..6.1.5..
5.1.m:
In the country of Ānarta there is a forest, a shelter for sages,
charming to all living beings, whose trees bear fruit in all seasons.

5.1.s:
tatrāśramapadaṃ ramyaṃ saumyasattvaniṣevitam..
asti tāpasasaṃkīrṇaṃ vedadhvanivirājitam..6.1.6..
5.1.d:
तत्राश्रमपदं रम्यं सौम्यसत्त्वनिषेवितम्..
अस्ति तापससंकीर्णं वेदध्वनिविराजितम्..6.1.6..
5.1.m:
There is a lovely hermitage frequented by gentle creatures,
filled with ascetics, radiant with the sound of the Vedas,

5.1.s:
abbhakṣairvāyubhakṣaiśca śīrṇaparṇāśibhistathā.
dantolūkhalibhirvipraiḥ sevitaṃ cāśmakuṭṭakaiḥ..6.1.7..
5.1.d:
अब्भक्षैर्वायुभक्षैश्च शीर्णपर्णाशिभिस्तथा.
दन्तोलूखलिभिर्विप्रैः सेवितं चाश्मकुट्टकैः..6.1.7..
5.1.m:
frequented by brahmins living on water, living on air, eating fallen leaves,
using teeth as mortars, and using stones as pounders,

5.1.s:
snānahomaparaiścaiva japasvādhyāyatatparaiḥ.
vānaprasthaistridaṇḍaiśca haṃsaiścāpi kuṭīcaraiḥ..6.1.8..
5.1.d:
स्नानहोमपरैश्चैव जपस्वाध्यायतत्परैः.
वानप्रस्थैस्त्रिदण्डैश्च हंसैश्चापि कुटीचरैः..6.1.8..
5.1.m:
devoted to ritual ablution and fire oblations, intent on recitation and daily study,
forest-dwellers, triple-staff ascetics, and haṃsas and kuṭīcaras,

5.1.s:
snātakairyatibhirdāntaistathā paṃcāgnisādhakaiḥ.
kasyacittvatha kālasya bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ..6.1.9..
5.1.d:
स्नातकैर्यतिभिर्दान्तैस्तथा पंचाग्निसाधकैः.
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य भगवांस्त्रिपुरांतकः..6.1.9..
5.1.m:
snātakas, disciplined ascetics, and practitioners of the five fires.
Then, after some time, the blessed destroyer of Tripura,

5.1.s:
satīviyogasaṃtapto bhramamāṇa itastataḥ.
tasminvane samāyātaḥ saumyasattvaniṣevite..6.1.10..
5.1.d:
सतीवियोगसंतप्तो भ्रममाण इतस्ततः.
तस्मिन्वने समायातः सौम्यसत्त्वनिषेविते..6.1.10..
5.1.m:
tormented by separation from Satī, wandering here and there,
arrived in that forest frequented by gentle creatures,

5.1.s:
krīḍaṃti nakulā yatra sārdhaṃ sarpaiḥpraharṣitāḥ.
pañcānanāśca mātaṃgairvṛṣadaṃśāstathākhubhiḥ.
kākāḥ kauśikasaṃghaiśca vairabhāvavivarjitāḥ..6.1.11..
5.1.d:
क्रीडंति नकुला यत्र सार्धं सर्पैःप्रहर्षिताः.
पञ्चाननाश्च मातंगैर्वृषदंशास्तथाखुभिः.
काकाः कौशिकसंघैश्च वैरभावविवर्जिताः..6.1.11..
5.1.m:
where mongooses play delightfully together with snakes,
lions with elephants, cats with mice,
and crows with flocks of owls, entirely free from enmity.

5.1.s:
tataśca bhagavānrudro dṛṣṭvāśramapadaṃ tadā.
nagnaḥ kapālamādāya bhikṣārthaṃ praviveśa saḥ..6.1.12..
5.1.d:
ततश्च भगवान्रुद्रो दृष्ट्वाश्रमपदं तदा.
नग्नः कपालमादाय भिक्षार्थं प्रविवेश सः..6.1.12..
5.1.m:
Then the blessed Rudra, seeing that hermitage,
entered naked, taking a skull-bowl to seek alms.

5.1.s:
atha tasya samālokya rūpaṃ gātrasamudbhavam.
adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ tāpasyaḥ sarvāḥ kāmavaśaṃ gatāḥ..6.1.13..
5.1.d:
अथ तस्य समालोक्य रूपं गात्रसमुद्भवम्.
अदृष्टपूर्वं तापस्यः सर्वाः कामवशं गताः..6.1.13..
5.1.m:
Then, beholding the form manifested in his limbs,
never seen before, all the ascetic women fell under the sway of desire.

5.1.s:
gṛhakarma parityajya guruśuśrūṣaṇāni ca.
mithaḥ saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ cakruḥ sthānesthāne ca tāḥ sthitāḥ..6.1.14..
5.1.d:
गृहकर्म परित्यज्य गुरुशुश्रूषणानि च.
मिथः संभाषणं चक्रुः स्थानेस्थाने च ताः स्थिताः..6.1.14..
5.1.m:
Abandoning household chores and attendance upon their elders,
standing here and there, they conversed with one another.

5.1.s:
ekā sā kāpi dhanyā yā cakre tasyāvagūhanam.
viśrabdhā sarvagātreṣu tāpasasya mahātmanaḥ..6.1.15..
5.1.d:
एका सा कापि धन्या या चक्रे तस्यावगूहनम्.
विश्रब्धा सर्वगात्रेषु तापसस्य महात्मनः..6.1.15..
5.1.m:
A certain fortunate woman embraced him;
trusting, [she pressed herself] against all the limbs of that great-souled ascetic.

5.1.s:
tathānyāḥ kautukāviṣṭā dhāvaṃtyaḥ sarvatodiśam.
dṛśyaṃte taṃ samuddiśya vistāritavilocanāḥ..6.1.16..
5.1.d:
तथान्याः कौतुकाविष्टा धावंत्यः सर्वतोदिशम्.
दृश्यंते तं समुद्दिश्य विस्तारितविलोचनाः..6.1.16..
5.1.m:
Likewise, other women filled with fascination, running in all directions,
were seen looking at him with wide-open eyes:

5.1.s:
kāścidarddhānuliptāṃgyaḥ kāścidekāṃjitekṣaṇāḥ.
ardhasaṃyamitaiḥ kaiśaistathānyāstyaktabālakāḥ..6.1.17..
5.1.d:
काश्चिदर्द्धानुलिप्तांग्यः काश्चिदेकांजितेक्षणाः.
अर्धसंयमितैः कैशैस्तथान्यास्त्यक्तबालकाः..6.1.17..
5.1.m:
some with their limbs half-anointed, some with collyrium in only one eye,
with hair half-tied up, and others leaving their children behind.

5.1.s:
evamālokyamānaḥ sa kāminībhirmaheśvaraḥ.
babhrāma rājamārgeṇa bhikṣāṃ dehīti kīrtayan..6.1.18..
5.1.d:
एवमालोक्यमानः स कामिनीभिर्महेश्वरः.
बभ्राम राजमार्गेण भिक्षां देहीति कीर्तयन्..6.1.18..
5.1.m:
Being thus gazed upon by the enamoured women, Maheśvara
wandered along the main road, calling out, "Give alms!"

5.1.s:
atha te munayo dṛṣṭvā taṃ tathā vigatāṃbaram.
kāmodbhavakaraṃstrīṇāṃ procuḥ kopāruṇekṣaṇāḥ..6.1.19..
5.1.d:
अथ ते मुनयो दृष्ट्वा तं तथा विगतांबरम्.
कामोद्भवकरंस्त्रीणां प्रोचुः कोपारुणेक्षणाः..6.1.19..
5.1.m:
Then those sages, seeing him thus unclad,
arousing passion in the women, their eyes red with anger, said:

5.1.s:
yasmātpāpa tvayāsmākamāśramo'yaṃ viḍaṃbitaḥ.
tasmālliṃgaṃ patatvāśu tavaiva vasudhātale..6.1.20..
5.1.d:
यस्मात्पाप त्वयास्माकमाश्रमोऽयं विडंबितः.
तस्माल्लिंगं पतत्वाशु तवैव वसुधातले..6.1.20..
5.1.m:
"Since our hermitage has been mocked by you, you wicked one,
therefore let your liṅga immediately fall onto the surface of the earth!"

5.1.s:
etasminnaṃtare bhūmau liṃgaṃ tasya papāta tat.
bhittvātha dharaṇīpṛṣṭhaṃ pātālaṃ praviveśa ha..6.1.21..
5.1.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे भूमौ लिंगं तस्य पपात तत्.
भित्त्वाथ धरणीपृष्ठं पातालं प्रविवेश ह..6.1.21..
5.1.m:
At that very moment, that liṅga of his fell upon the earth;
and having split the surface of the ground, it entered Pātāla.

5.1.s:
so'pi liṃgaparityakto lajjāyukto maheśvaraḥ.
gartāṃ gurvīṃ samāśritya bhrūṇarūpaḥ samāviśat..6.1.22..
5.1.d:
सोऽपि लिंगपरित्यक्तो लज्जायुक्तो महेश्वरः.
गर्तां गुर्वीं समाश्रित्य भ्रूणरूपः समाविशत्..6.1.22..
5.1.m:
He too, bereft of his liṅga and filled with shame, Maheśvara,
took shelter in a deep cavity and entered it in the form of an embryo.

5.1.s:
atha liṃgasya pātena trailokyabhayaśaṃsinaḥ.
utpātā dāruṇāstasthuḥ sarvatra dvijasattamāḥ..6.1.23..
5.1.d:
अथ लिंगस्य पातेन त्रैलोक्यभयशंसिनः.
उत्पाता दारुणास्तस्थुः सर्वत्र द्विजसत्तमाः..6.1.23..
5.1.m:
Then, due to the falling of the liṅga, terrifying portents
heralding fear for the three worlds occurred everywhere, O best of the twice-born.

5.1.s:
śīryate giriśṛṅgāṇi pataṃtyulkā divāpi ca.
tyajaṃti sāgarāḥ sarve maryādāṃ ca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ..6.1.24..
5.1.d:
शीर्यते गिरिशृङ्गाणि पतंत्युल्का दिवापि च.
त्यजंति सागराः सर्वे मर्यादां च शनैः शनैः..6.1.24..
5.1.m:
Mountain peaks crumble, meteors fall even by day,
and all the oceans gradually abandon their bounds.

5.1.s:
atha devagaṇāḥ sarve bhayasaṃtrastamānasāḥ.
śakraviṣṇumukhā jagmuryatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ..6.1.25..
5.1.d:
अथ देवगणाः सर्वे भयसंत्रस्तमानसाः.
शक्रविष्णुमुखा जग्मुर्यत्र देवः पितामहः..6.1.25..
5.1.m:
Then all the hosts of gods, their minds terrified with dread,
led by Śakra and Viṣṇu, went to where the god Pitāmaha was.

5.1.s:
procuśca praṇatāḥ stutvā stotraiḥ suśrutisaṃbhavaiḥ.
trailokye sṛṣṭirūpaṃ yatkamalāsanasaṃsthitam..6.1.26..
5.1.d:
प्रोचुश्च प्रणताः स्तुत्वा स्तोत्रैः सुश्रुतिसंभवैः.
त्रैलोक्ये सृष्टिरूपं यत्कमलासनसंस्थितम्..6.1.26..
5.1.m:
Having bowed down and praised him with hymns derived from the fine scriptures,
they spoke to him who is seated on a lotus throne, the creator in the three worlds:

5.1.s:
kimidaṃ kimidaṃ deva vartate hyadharottaram.
trailokyaṃ sakalaṃ yena vyākulatvamupāgatam..6.1.27..
5.1.d:
किमिदं किमिदं देव वर्तते ह्यधरोत्तरम्.
त्रैलोक्यं सकलं येन व्याकुलत्वमुपागतम्..6.1.27..
5.1.m:
"What is this, O Lord, what is this topsy-turvy state that has arisen,
by which the entire threefold world has been thrown into distress?

5.1.s:
pralayasyeva cihnāni dṛśyaṃte padmasaṃbhava.
kiṃ sāṃpratamakāle'pi bhaviṣyati parikṣayaḥ..6.1.28..
5.1.d:
प्रलयस्येव चिह्नानि दृश्यंते पद्मसंभव.
किं सांप्रतमकालेऽपि भविष्यति परिक्षयः..6.1.28..
5.1.m:
Signs like those of the cosmic dissolution are seen, O lotus-born one.
Will there now be untimely destruction?

5.1.s:
sarveṣāṃ suramartyānāṃ daityānāṃ mantrakovidaḥ.
gatirbhayārtadehānāṃ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ..6.1.29..
5.1.d:
सर्वेषां सुरमर्त्यानां दैत्यानां मन्त्रकोविदः.
गतिर्भयार्तदेहानां सर्वलोकपितामहः..6.1.29..
5.1.m:
O knower of mantras, the refuge of all gods, mortals, and Daityas
whose bodies are afflicted by fear, the grandfather of all the worlds!"

5.1.s:
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ caturānanaḥ.
uvāca suciraṃ dhyātvā jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā..6.1.30..
5.1.d:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां चतुराननः.
उवाच सुचिरं ध्यात्वा ज्ञात्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा..6.1.30..
5.1.m:
Hearing those words of the gods, the four-faced one,
having meditated for a long time and understood through his divine eye, spoke:

5.1.s:
pralayasya na kālo'yaṃ sāṃprataṃ surasattamāḥ.
śṛṇudhvaṃ yannimittotthā mahotpātā bhavantyamī..6.1.31..
5.1.d:
प्रलयस्य न कालोऽयं सांप्रतं सुरसत्तमाः.
शृणुध्वं यन्निमित्तोत्था महोत्पाता भवन्त्यमी..6.1.31..
5.1.m:
"This is not the time of cosmic dissolution now, O best of the gods.
Listen to the reason from which these great portents have arisen:

5.1.s:
ṛṣibhiḥ pātitaṃ liṃgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ.
śāpenānartake deśe kalatrārthe mahātmabhiḥ..6.1.32..
5.1.d:
ऋषिभिः पातितं लिंगं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः.
शापेनानर्तके देशे कलत्रार्थे महात्मभिः..6.1.32..
5.1.m:
The liṅga of the god of gods, the spear-wielder, was caused to fall
by the great-souled seers through a curse in the land of Ānarta, on account of their wives.

5.1.s:
tenaitadvyākulībhūtaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram.
tasmādgacchāmahe tatra yatra devo maheśvaraḥ..6.1.33..
5.1.d:
तेनैतद्व्याकुलीभूतं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्.
तस्माद्गच्छामहे तत्र यत्र देवो महेश्वरः..6.1.33..
5.1.m:
Because of that, this threefold world, with all that moves and is still, has become agitated.
Therefore, let us go there, where the god Maheśvara is,

5.1.s:
yenāsmadvacanācchīghraṃ talliṃgaṃ nidadhāti saḥ.
no cedbhaviṣyati vyaktamakāle cāpi saṃkṣayaḥ.
trailokyasyāpi kṛtsnasya satyametanmayoditam..6.1.34..
5.1.d:
येनास्मद्वचनाच्छीघ्रं तल्लिंगं निदधाति सः.
नो चेद्भविष्यति व्यक्तमकाले चापि संक्षयः.
त्रैलोक्यस्यापि कृत्स्नस्य सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम्..6.1.34..
5.1.m:
so that, at our word, he may quickly set that liṅga [in place] again.
Otherwise, untimely destruction will visibly come to pass
for the entire three worlds as well; this that I have spoken is true."

5.1.s:
atha devagaṇāḥ sarve brahmaviṣṇupuraḥsarāḥ.
ādityā vasavo rudrā viśvedevāstathāśvinau..6.1.35..
5.1.d:
अथ देवगणाः सर्वे ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरःसराः.
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा विश्वेदेवास्तथाश्विनौ..6.1.35..
5.1.m:
Then all the hosts of gods, headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu,
the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Viśvedevas, and the Aśvins,

5.1.s:
prajagmustvaritāstatra yatra devo maheśvaraḥ.
gartāmadhyagataḥ supto lajjayā parayā vṛtaḥ..6.1.36..
5.1.d:
प्रजग्मुस्त्वरितास्तत्र यत्र देवो महेश्वरः.
गर्तामध्यगतः सुप्तो लज्जया परया वृतः..6.1.36..
5.1.m:
hastily went to where the god Maheśvara was,
lying asleep within a pit, enveloped in great shame.

5.1.s:
devā ūcuḥ.
namaste devadeveśa bhaktānāmabhayaprada.
namaste jagadādhāra śaśirājitaśekhara..6.1.37..
5.1.d:
देवा ऊचुः.
नमस्ते देवदेवेश भक्तानामभयप्रद.
नमस्ते जगदाधार शशिराजितशेखर..6.1.37..
5.1.m:
The gods said:
"Homage to you, O Lord of the god of gods, who grant fearlessness to devotees!
Homage to you, O support of the universe, whose crest is adorned by the moon!

5.1.s:
tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvamāpastvaṃ mahī vibho.
tvayā sṛṣṭamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram..6.1.38..
5.1.d:
त्वं यज्ञस्त्वं वषट्कारस्त्वमापस्त्वं मही विभो.
त्वया सृष्टमिदं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्..6.1.38..
5.1.m:
You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the waters, you are the earth, O all-pervading Lord!
By you was this entire threefold world created, with all that moves and is still.

5.1.s:
tvaṃ pāsi ca suraśreṣṭha tathā nāśaṃ nayiṣyasi.
tvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ caturvaktrastvaṃ caṃdrastvaṃ divākaraḥ..6.1.39..
5.1.d:
त्वं पासि च सुरश्रेष्ठ तथा नाशं नयिष्यसि.
त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं चतुर्वक्त्रस्त्वं चंद्रस्त्वं दिवाकरः..6.1.39..
5.1.m:
You protect, O best of gods, and likewise you lead to destruction.
You are Viṣṇu, you are the four-faced one, you are the moon, you are the sun.

5.1.s:
tvayā vinā mahādeva na kiṃcidiha vidyate.
api kṛtvā mahatpāpaṃ naro deva dharātale..6.1.40..
5.1.d:
त्वया विना महादेव न किंचिदिह विद्यते.
अपि कृत्वा महत्पापं नरो देव धरातले..6.1.40..
5.1.m:
Without you, O Mahādeva, nothing exists here.
Even having committed a great sin, a man on the surface of the earth, O Lord—"

5.1.s:
tava nāmāpi saṃkīrtya prayāti tridivālayam.
mahādeva mahādeva mahādeveti kīrtanāt..6.1.41..
5.1.d:
तव नामापि संकीर्त्य प्रयाति त्रिदिवालयम्.
महादेव महादेव महादेवेति कीर्तनात्..6.1.41..
5.1.m: even by chanting your name, he goes to heaven, the abode of the gods. / From the chanting of "Mahādeva, Mahādeva, Mahādeva",

5.1.s:
koṭayo brahmahatyānāmagamyāgamakoṭayaḥ.
sadyaḥ pralayamāyāṃti mahādeveti kīrtanāt..6.1.42..
5.1.d:
कोटयो ब्रह्महत्यानामगम्यागमकोटयः.
सद्यः प्रलयमायांति महादेवेति कीर्तनात्..6.1.42..
5.1.m: crores of murders of brahmins and crores of incestuous relations / are dissolved immediately, from the recitation: "Mahādeva!"

5.1.s:
vipro yathā manuṣyāṇāṃ nadīnāṃ vā mahārṇavaḥ.
tathā tvaṃ sarvadevānāmādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ..6.1.43..
5.1.d:
विप्रो यथा मनुष्याणां नदीनां वा महार्णवः.
तथा त्वं सर्वदेवानामाधिपत्ये व्यवस्थितः..6.1.43..
5.1.m: Just as the brahmin stands supreme among men, or the great ocean among rivers, / so do you stand in sovereignty over all the gods.

5.1.s:
nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathā caṃdraḥ pradīptānāṃ divākaraḥ.
tathā tvaṃ sarvadevānāmādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ..6.1.44..
5.1.d:
नक्षत्राणां यथा चंद्रः प्रदीप्तानां दिवाकरः.
तथा त्वं सर्वदेवानामाधिपत्ये व्यवस्थितः..6.1.44..
5.1.m: Just as the moon stands supreme among the asterisms, and the sun among luminous bodies, / so do you stand in sovereignty over all the gods.

5.1.s:
dhātūnāṃ kāṃcanaṃ yadvadgaṃdharvāṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ.
tathā tvaṃ sarvadevānāmādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ..6.1.45..
5.1.d:
धातूनां कांचनं यद्वद्गंधर्वाणां च नारदः.
तथा त्वं सर्वदेवानामाधिपत्ये व्यवस्थितः..6.1.45..
5.1.m: Just as gold stands supreme among metals, and Nārada among the gandharvas, / so do you stand in sovereignty over all the gods.

5.1.s:
oṣadhīnāṃ yathā sasyaṃ nagānāṃ hemaparvataḥ.
tathā tvaṃ sarvadevānāmādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ..6.1.46..
5.1.d:
ओषधीनां यथा सस्यं नगानां हेमपर्वतः.
तथा त्वं सर्वदेवानामाधिपत्ये व्यवस्थितः..6.1.46..
5.1.m: Just as cultivated grain stands supreme among plants, and the golden mountain [Meru] among mountains, / so do you stand in sovereignty over all the gods.

5.1.s:
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ naḥ sarveṣāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ vibho.
saṃdhāraya punarliṃgaṃ svakīyaṃ surasattama..6.1.47..
5.1.d:
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं नः सर्वेषां च नृणां विभो.
संधारय पुनर्लिंगं स्वकीयं सुरसत्तम..6.1.47..
5.1.m: Therefore, show grace to us and to all human beings, O all-pervading lord; / take up your own liṅga once again, O best of the gods.

5.1.s:
nocejjagattrayaṃ deva nūnaṃ nāśamamupeṣyati.
yadyetadbhūtale liṅgaṃ patati sthāsyati prabho..6.1.48..
5.1.d:
नोचेज्जगत्त्रयं देव नूनं नाशममुपेष्यति.
यद्येतद्भूतले लिङ्गं पतति स्थास्यति प्रभो..6.1.48..
5.1.m: Otherwise, O lord, the three worlds will surely meet destruction / if this liṅga falls and remains upon the surface of the earth, O master.

5.1.s:
sūta uvāca.
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhagavānbṛṣabhadhvajaḥ.
provāca praṇatānsarvāṃstāndevānvrīḍayānvitaḥ..6.1.49..
5.1.d:
सूत उवाच.
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भगवान्बृषभध्वजः.
प्रोवाच प्रणतान्सर्वांस्तान्देवान्व्रीडयान्वितः..6.1.49..
5.1.m: Sūta said: / Hearing that speech of theirs, the blessed lord whose banner bears a bull, / filled with modesty, spoke to all those gods who stood bowing down:

5.1.s:
mayā satīviyogārtiyuktena surasattama.
liṃgametatparityaktaṃ śāpavyājāddvijanmanām..6.1.50..
5.1.d:
मया सतीवियोगार्तियुक्तेन सुरसत्तम.
लिंगमेतत्परित्यक्तं शापव्याजाद्द्विजन्मनाम्..6.1.50..
5.1.m: "Afflicted with the agony of separation from Satī, O best of the gods, / this liṅga was cast away by me under the pretext of the curse of the twice-born.

5.1.s:
ko'laṃ pātayituṃ liṃgaṃ mamaitadbhuvanatraye.
devo vā brāhmaṇo vāpi vettha yūyamapi sphuṭam..6.1.51..
5.1.d:
कोऽलं पातयितुं लिंगं ममैतद्भुवनत्रये.
देवो वा ब्राह्मणो वापि वेत्थ यूयमपि स्फुटम्..6.1.51..
5.1.m: Who in the three worlds is capable of causing my liṅga to fall, / be it a god or even a brahmin? You too know this clearly.

5.1.s:
tasmānnaiva dhariṣyāmi liṃgametaddharātalāt.
kimanena kariṣyāmi bhāryayā parivarjitaḥ..6.1.52..
5.1.d:
तस्मान्नैव धरिष्यामि लिंगमेतद्धरातलात्.
किमनेन करिष्यामि भार्यया परिवर्जितः..6.1.52..
5.1.m: Therefore, I shall not take up this liṅga from the earth's surface. / Deprived of my wife, what will I do with it?"

5.1.s:
devā ūcuḥ.
tava kāṃtā satī nāma yā mṛtā prāksurottama.
sā jātā menakāgarbhe gaurī nāma himācalāt..6.1.53..
5.1.d:
देवा ऊचुः.
तव कांता सती नाम या मृता प्राक्सुरोत्तम.
सा जाता मेनकागर्भे गौरी नाम हिमाचलात्..6.1.53..
5.1.m: The gods said: / "She who was your beloved, named Satī, who previously died, O best of the gods, / has been born from Himācala in the womb of Menakā under the name Gaurī.

5.1.s:
bhaviṣyati punarbhāryā tavaiva tripurāṃtaka.
tasmālliṃgaṃ samādāya kuru kṣemaṃ divaukasām..6.1.54..
5.1.d:
भविष्यति पुनर्भार्या तवैव त्रिपुरांतक.
तस्माल्लिंगं समादाय कुरु क्षेमं दिवौकसाम्..6.1.54..
5.1.m: She will once again become your wife, O destroyer of Tripura. / Therefore, take up your liṅga and grant well-being to the gods."

5.1.s:
devadeva uvāca.
adyaprabhṛti me liṃgaṃ yadi devā dvijātayaḥ.
pūjayaṃti prayatnena tarhīdaṃ dhārayāmyaham..6.1.55..
5.1.d:
देवदेव उवाच.
अद्यप्रभृति मे लिंगं यदि देवा द्विजातयः.
पूजयंति प्रयत्नेन तर्हीदं धारयाम्यहम्..6.1.55..
5.1.m: The god of gods said: / "If from this day forward the gods and the twice-born / worship my liṅga with devotion, then I shall take it up."

5.1.s:
brahmovāca.
ahaṃ tava svayaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi śaṃkara.
tathānye vibudhāḥ sarve kiṃ punarbhuvi mānavāḥ..6.1.56..
5.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच.
अहं तव स्वयं लिंगं पूजयिष्यामि शंकर.
तथान्ये विबुधाः सर्वे किं पुनर्भुवि मानवाः..6.1.56..
5.1.m: Brahmā said: / "I myself will worship your liṅga, O Śaṃkara, / and so will all the other gods; how much more so mortals upon earth!"

5.1.s:
tataḥ praviśya pātālaṃ devaiḥ sārdhaṃ pitāmahaḥ.
svayamevākarotpūjāṃ tasya liṃgasya bhaktitaḥ..6.1.57..
5.1.d:
ततः प्रविश्य पातालं देवैः सार्धं पितामहः.
स्वयमेवाकरोत्पूजां तस्य लिंगस्य भक्तितः..6.1.57..
5.1.m: Then, having entered Pātāla along with the gods, the Grandsire / himself worshiped that liṅga with devotion.

5.1.s:
tasmādanaṃtaraṃ viṣṇuḥ śraddhāpūtena cetasā.
tathānye vibudhāḥ sarve śakrādyāḥ śraddhayānvitāḥ..6.1.58..
5.1.d:
तस्मादनंतरं विष्णुः श्रद्धापूतेन चेतसा.
तथान्ये विबुधाः सर्वे शक्राद्याः श्रद्धयान्विताः..6.1.58..
5.1.m: Immediately after him, Viṣṇu [worshiped it] with a mind purified by faith, / and likewise all the other gods headed by Śakra, filled with faith.

5.1.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādevaḥ pitāmahamidaṃ vacaḥ.
provāca vāsudevaṃ ca vinayāvanataṃ sthitam..6.1.59..
5.1.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवः पितामहमिदं वचः.
प्रोवाच वासुदेवं च विनयावनतं स्थितम्..6.1.59..
5.1.m: Then Mahādeva, well-pleased, spoke these words / to the Grandsire and to Vāsudeva who stood bowed in humility:

5.1.s:
bhavadbhyāṃ parituṣṭo'smi tasmānmattaḥ pragṛhyatām.
varamiṣṭaṃ mahābhāgau yadyapi syātsudurlabham..6.1.60..
5.1.d:
भवद्भ्यां परितुष्टोऽस्मि तस्मान्मत्तः प्रगृह्यताम्.
वरमिष्टं महाभागौ यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभम्..6.1.60..
5.1.m: "I am greatly pleased with both of you; therefore, receive from me / the desired boon, O fortunate ones, even if it be very difficult to attain."

5.1.s:
tāvūcatuḥ.
yadi tuṣṭosi deveśa tribhāgena samāśrayam.
āvābhyāṃ dehi liṃgena yenaikatrāśrayo bhavet..6.1.61..
5.1.d:
तावूचतुः.
यदि तुष्टोसि देवेश त्रिभागेन समाश्रयम्.
आवाभ्यां देहि लिंगेन येनैकत्राश्रयो भवेत्..6.1.61..
5.1.m: The two of them said: / "If you are pleased, O lord of gods, grant through your liṅga / an abode divided into three parts for both of us, so that there may be a shared dwelling in one place."

5.1.s:
sūta uvāca.
sa tatheti pratijñāya liṃgamādāya ca prabhuḥ.
sthāne niyojayāmāsa sarvadevādhipūjitam..6.1.62..
5.1.d:
सूत उवाच.
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय लिंगमादाय च प्रभुः.
स्थाने नियोजयामास सर्वदेवाधिपूजितम्..6.1.62..
5.1.m: Sūta said: / Having agreed, saying, 'So be it,' the master took up the liṅga, / worshiped by all the lords of the gods, and installed it in its place.

5.1.s:
tato hāṭakamādāya tadākāraṃ pitāmahaḥ.
kṛtvā liṃgaṃ svayaṃ tatra sthāpayāmāsa harṣitaḥ..6.1.63..
5.1.d:
ततो हाटकमादाय तदाकारं पितामहः.
कृत्वा लिंगं स्वयं तत्र स्थापयामास हर्षितः..6.1.63..
5.1.m: Then, taking gold, the Grandsire fashioned a liṅga / of that very form and himself joyfully installed it there.

5.1.s:
provāca cātha bho viprāḥ sādhunādena nādayan.
lokatrayaṃ samastānāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tridivaukasām..6.1.64..
5.1.d:
प्रोवाच चाथ भो विप्राः साधुनादेन नादयन्.
लोकत्रयं समस्तानां शृण्वतां त्रिदिवौकसाम्..6.1.64..
5.1.m: Then he spoke, O brahmins, making the three worlds resound / with a loud proclamation, while all the celestial beings listened:

5.1.s:
mayā hyādyaṃ tvidaṃ liṃgaṃ hāṭakena vinirmitam.
khyātiṃ yāsyati sarvatra pātāle hāṭakeśvaram..6.1.65..
5.1.d:
मया ह्याद्यं त्विदं लिंगं हाटकेन विनिर्मितम्.
ख्यातिं यास्यति सर्वत्र पाताले हाटकेश्वरम्..6.1.65..
5.1.m: "Indeed, this first liṅga was fashioned by me from gold (hāṭaka); / it will attain fame everywhere in Pātāla as Hāṭakeśvara.

5.1.s:
tathānye manujā ye ca hāṭakādīni bhaktitaḥ.
maṇimuktāsuratnaiśca kṛtvā liṃgāni kṛtsnaśaḥ..6.1.66..
5.1.d:
तथान्ये मनुजा ये च हाटकादीनि भक्तितः.
मणिमुक्तासुरत्नैश्च कृत्वा लिंगानि कृत्स्नशः..6.1.66..
5.1.m: Likewise, whichever other mortals out of devotion fashion liṅgas / from gold and other materials, and entirely of jewels, pearls, and precious gems,

5.1.s:
trikālaṃ pūjayiṣyaṃti te yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim.
mṛnmayaṃ saṃparityajya nīcadhātumayaṃ tathā..6.1.67..
5.1.d:
त्रिकालं पूजयिष्यंति ते यास्यंति परां गतिम्.
मृन्मयं संपरित्यज्य नीचधातुमयं तथा..6.1.67..
5.1.m: and worship them at the three junctures of the day, leaving aside what is made of clay / and what is made of base metal, they will attain the supreme state."

5.1.s:
evamuktvā caturvaktraḥ saha sarvairdivālayaiḥ.
jagāma tridivaṃ so'pi kailāsaṃ śaśiśekharaḥ..6.1.68..
5.1.d:
एवमुक्त्वा चतुर्वक्त्रः सह सर्वैर्दिवालयैः.
जगाम त्रिदिवं सोऽपि कैलासं शशिशेखरः..6.1.68..
5.1.m: Having spoken thus, the four-faced [Brahmā] went to heaven along with all the gods, / and the moon-crested lord went to Kailāsa.

5.1.s:
etasmātkāraṇālliṃgaṃ pūjyate'tra surāsuraiḥ.
harasya cottamāṃgāni parityajya viśeṣataḥ..6.1.69..
5.1.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाल्लिंगं पूज्यतेऽत्र सुरासुरैः.
हरस्य चोत्तमांगानि परित्यज्य विशेषतः..6.1.69..
5.1.m: For this reason, the liṅga of Hara is especially worshiped here / by gods and asuras, in preference to his superior limbs.

5.1.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti talliṃgaṃ svayaṃ brahmā vyavasthitaḥ.
bhagavānvāsudevaśca tena pūjyaṃ śivaṃ hi tat..6.1.70..
5.1.d:
ततः प्रभृति तल्लिंगं स्वयं ब्रह्मा व्यवस्थितः.
भगवान्वासुदेवश्च तेन पूज्यं शिवं हि तत्..6.1.70..
5.1.m: From that time forth, Brahmā himself and the blessed Vāsudeva / have taken up residence in that liṅga; therefore is that auspicious [symbol of] Śiva worshipful.

5.1.s:
yastu pūjayate nityaṃ śraddhāyuktena cetasā.
tryaṃbakācyutabrahmādyāstena syuḥ pūjitāstrayaḥ..6.1.71..
5.1.d:
यस्तु पूजयते नित्यं श्रद्धायुक्तेन चेतसा.
त्र्यंबकाच्युतब्रह्माद्यास्तेन स्युः पूजितास्त्रयः..6.1.71..
5.1.m: He who continually worships it with a faithful heart / worships those three: the three-eyed Rudra, Acyuta, and Brahmā.

5.1.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena śivaliṃgaṃ prapūjayet.
sparśayedīkṣayennityaṃ kīrtayecca dvijottamāḥ..6.1.72..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye liṃgotpattivarṇanaṃ nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ..1..
5.1.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन शिवलिंगं प्रपूजयेत्.
स्पर्शयेदीक्षयेन्नित्यं कीर्तयेच्च द्विजोत्तमाः..6.1.72..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये लिंगोत्पत्तिवर्णनं नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः..1..
5.1.m:
Therefore, by every effort one should worship the Śivaliṅga, / touch it, look upon it daily, and praise it, O best of the twice-born.
Thus ends the first chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the Liṅga,' in the section on the greatness of Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the sixth part of the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.2.s:
sūta uvāca.
tasminnutpāṭite liṃge bhūtalāddvijasattamāḥ.
pātālājjāhnavītoyaṃ tena mārgeṇa niḥsṛtam.
sarvapāpaharaṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvakāmapradāyakam..6.2.1..
5.2.d:
सूत उवाच.
तस्मिन्नुत्पाटिते लिंगे भूतलाद्द्विजसत्तमाः.
पातालाज्जाह्नवीतोयं तेन मार्गेण निःसृतम्.
सर्वपापहरं नॄणां सर्वकामप्रदायकम्..6.2.1..
5.2.m: Sūta said: / When that liṅga was uprooted from the earth's surface, O best of the twice-born, / through that channel the waters of the Jāhnavī issued forth from Pātāla, / destroying all sins of men and granting every desire.

5.2.s:
tatra svayamabhūtpūrvaṃ yattaddvijavarottamāḥ.
śṛṇudhvaṃ vadato me'dya lokavismayakārakam..6.2.2..
5.2.d:
तत्र स्वयमभूत्पूर्वं यत्तद्द्विजवरोत्तमाः.
शृणुध्वं वदतो मेऽद्य लोकविस्मयकारकम्..6.2.2..
5.2.m: Listen now as I relate what previously occurred there by itself, / O best of noble twice-born, which brought wonder to the world.

5.2.s:
triśaṃkurnāma rājeṃdraścaṃḍālatvaṃ samāgataḥ.
tatra snātaḥ punarlebhe śarīraṃ pārthivocitam..6.2.3..
5.2.d:
त्रिशंकुर्नाम राजेंद्रश्चंडालत्वं समागतः.
तत्र स्नातः पुनर्लेभे शरीरं पार्थिवोचितम्..6.2.3..
5.2.m: A king of kings named Triśaṅku was reduced to the status of a caṇḍāla; / having bathed there, he regained a body worthy of an earthly king.

5.2.s:
ṛṣayaḥ ūcuḥ.
caṃḍālatvaṃ kathaṃ prāptastriśaṃkurnṛpasattamaḥ.
etattvaṃ sarvamācakṣva vistarātsūtanandana..6.2.4..
5.2.d:
ऋषयः ऊचुः.
चंडालत्वं कथं प्राप्तस्त्रिशंकुर्नृपसत्तमः.
एतत्त्वं सर्वमाचक्ष्व विस्तरात्सूतनन्दन..6.2.4..
5.2.m: The seers said: / How did Triśaṅku, that best of kings, come to be a caṇḍāla? / Tell us all this in detail, O son of Sūta.

5.2.s:
sūta uvāca.
ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ purātanīm.
sarvapāpaharāṃ medhyāṃ triśaṃkunṛpasaṃbhavām..6.2.5..
5.2.d:
सूत उवाच.
अहं वः कीर्तयिष्यामि कथामेतां पुरातनीम्.
सर्वपापहरां मेध्यां त्रिशंकुनृपसंभवाम्..6.2.5..
5.2.m: Sūta said: / I will narrate to you this ancient, holy story / that removes all sins, concerning King Triśaṅku.

5.2.s:
sūryavaṃśodbhavaḥ pūrvaṃ triśaṃkuriti viśrutaḥ.
āsītpārthivaśārdūlaḥ śārdūlasamavikramaḥ..6.2.6..
5.2.d:
सूर्यवंशोद्भवः पूर्वं त्रिशंकुरिति विश्रुतः.
आसीत्पार्थिवशार्दूलः शार्दूलसमविक्रमः..6.2.6..
5.2.m: Born in the solar dynasty, there was previously a famous king, / a tiger among earth-rulers, named Triśaṅku, whose prowess equaled that of a tiger.

5.2.s:
vasiṣṭhasya muneḥ śiṣyo yajvā dānapatiḥ prabhuḥ.
teneṣṭaṃ ca makhaiḥ sarvairagniṣṭomādibhiḥ sadā..6.2.7..
5.2.d:
वसिष्ठस्य मुनेः शिष्यो यज्वा दानपतिः प्रभुः.
तेनेष्टं च मखैः सर्वैरग्निष्टोमादिभिः सदा..6.2.7..
5.2.m: A disciple of the sage Vasiṣṭha, he was a performer of sacrifices, a generous giver, and a ruler; / he continually sacrificed with all sacrifices, beginning with the Agniṣṭoma,

5.2.s:
saṃpūrṇadakṣiṇaireva vatsaraṃ vatsaraṃ prati.
tathā dānāni sarvāṇi pradattāni mahātmanā..6.2.8..
5.2.d:
संपूर्णदक्षिणैरेव वत्सरं वत्सरं प्रति.
तथा दानानि सर्वाणि प्रदत्तानि महात्मना..6.2.8..
5.2.m: year after year, with bountiful priestly fees; / likewise, all kinds of gifts were bestowed by the great-souled king

5.2.s:
brāhmaṇebhyo viśiṣṭebhyo dīnebhyaśca viśeṣataḥ.
vratāni ca pracīrṇāni rakṣitāḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ..6.2.9..
5.2.d:
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशिष्टेभ्यो दीनेभ्यश्च विशेषतः.
व्रतानि च प्रचीर्णानि रक्षिताः शरणागताः..6.2.9..
5.2.m: on distinguished brahmins and especially on the destitute; / religious observances were strictly kept, and those seeking refuge were protected.

5.2.s:
putravallālitā lokāḥ śatravaśca niṣūditāḥ.
bhrāṃtāni bhūtale yāni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca.
tapasvibhyo yathākāmaṃ yacchatā vāṃchitaṃ dhanam..6.2.10..
5.2.d:
पुत्रवल्लालिता लोकाः शत्रवश्च निषूदिताः.
भ्रांतानि भूतले यानि तीर्थान्यायतनानि च.
तपस्विभ्यो यथाकामं यच्छता वांछितं धनम्..6.2.10..
5.2.m: The subjects were cherished like sons, and enemies were slain. / The sacred fords and temples on the face of the earth were visited, / as he bestowed upon ascetics whatever wealth they desired according to their wish.

5.2.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya vasiṣṭho bhagavānmuniḥ.
tena proktaḥ sabhāmadhye saṃsthito natipūrvakam..6.2.11..
5.2.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य वसिष्ठो भगवान्मुनिः.
तेन प्रोक्तः सभामध्ये संस्थितो नतिपूर्वकम्..6.2.11..
5.2.m: Then, at some time, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha / was addressed by him after bowing reverently, standing in the midst of the assembly:

5.2.s:
triśaṃkuruvāca.
bhagavanyaṣṭumicchāmi tena yajñena sāṃpratam.
gamyate tridivaṃ yena saśarīreṇa satvaram..6.2.12..
5.2.d:
त्रिशंकुरुवाच.
भगवन्यष्टुमिच्छामि तेन यज्ञेन सांप्रतम्.
गम्यते त्रिदिवं येन सशरीरेण सत्वरम्..6.2.12..
5.2.m: Triśaṅku said: / "Venerable one, I desire now to sacrifice with that sacrificial rite / by which heaven may be reached swiftly in this very body.

5.2.s:
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me saṃbhārānāhara drutam.
tasya yajñasya siddhyarthaṃ yathārhānbrāhmaṇāṃstathā..6.2.13..
5.2.d:
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं मे संभारानाहर द्रुतम्.
तस्य यज्ञस्य सिद्ध्यर्थं यथार्हान्ब्राह्मणांस्तथा..6.2.13..
5.2.m: Therefore show me favor; gather quickly the materials / and the worthy brahmins for the accomplishment of that sacrifice."

5.2.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca.
na sa kaścitkraturyena gamyate tridivaṃ nṛpa.
anenaiva śarīreṇa satyametadbravīmyaham..6.2.14..
5.2.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच.
न स कश्चित्क्रतुर्येन गम्यते त्रिदिवं नृप.
अनेनैव शरीरेण सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीम्यहम्..6.2.14..
5.2.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / "There is no sacrificial rite, O king, by which heaven may be attained / in this very body; I speak this truth.

5.2.s:
agniṣṭomādayo yajñā ye proktāḥ prāksvayaṃbhuvā.
anyadehāṃtare svargaḥ prāpyate taiḥ kṛtairnṛpa..6.2.15..
5.2.d:
अग्निष्टोमादयो यज्ञा ये प्रोक्ताः प्राक्स्वयंभुवा.
अन्यदेहांतरे स्वर्गः प्राप्यते तैः कृतैर्नृप..6.2.15..
5.2.m: The sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma, which were proclaimed of old by the self-manifest [Brahmā]— / by performing them, O king, heaven is attained only in another body.

5.2.s:
yadi vā pṛthivīpāla tvayā yajñaprabhāvataḥ.
pārthivo vā dvijo vātha vaiśyo vānyataro'pi vā..6.2.16..
5.2.d:
यदि वा पृथिवीपाल त्वया यज्ञप्रभावतः.
पार्थिवो वा द्विजो वाथ वैश्यो वान्यतरोऽपि वा..6.2.16..
5.2.m: Or else, O protector of the earth, if through the power of a sacrifice / any king, brahmin, vaiśya, or any other

5.2.s:
svayaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vāpi saṃjāto'tra dharātale.
svargaṃ gataḥ śarīreṇa sahitastatprakīrtaya..6.2.17..
5.2.d:
स्वयं दृष्टः श्रुतो वापि संजातोऽत्र धरातले.
स्वर्गं गतः शरीरेण सहितस्तत्प्रकीर्तय..6.2.17..
5.2.m: was seen or heard by you to have been born here on the earth's surface / and gone to heaven accompanied by his body, then proclaim it!"

5.2.s:
triśaṃkuruvāca.
nāsādhyaṃ vidyate brahmaṃstavāhaṃ vedmi tattvataḥ.
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me yathā syānmanasepsitam..6.2.18..
5.2.d:
त्रिशंकुरुवाच.
नासाध्यं विद्यते ब्रह्मंस्तवाहं वेद्मि तत्त्वतः.
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं मे यथा स्यान्मनसेप्सितम्..6.2.18..
5.2.m: Triśaṅku said: / "There is nothing impossible for you, O brahmin; I know this in truth. / Therefore show me favor, so that the desire of my heart may be fulfilled."

5.2.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca.
anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me svaireṣvapi hi jihvayā.
tasmānnāsti makhaḥ kaścitsatyaṃ tvaṃ yaṣṭumicchasi..6.2.19..
5.2.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच.
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे स्वैरेष्वपि हि जिह्वया.
तस्मान्नास्ति मखः कश्चित्सत्यं त्वं यष्टुमिच्छसि..6.2.19..
5.2.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / "An untruth has never before been spoken by my tongue, even in jest. / Therefore there is no sacrifice [such as] you truly wish to perform."

5.2.s:
triśaṃkuruvāca.
yadi māṃ vipraśārdūla na tvaṃ yājayituṃ kṣamaḥ.
svargapradena yajñena vapuṣānena vai vibho..6.2.20..
5.2.d:
त्रिशंकुरुवाच.
यदि मां विप्रशार्दूल न त्वं याजयितुं क्षमः.
स्वर्गप्रदेन यज्ञेन वपुषानेन वै विभो..6.2.20..
5.2.m: Triśaṅku said: / "If you are not capable, O tiger among brahmins, of officiating at a sacrifice for me— / a sacrifice bestowing heaven in this very body, O lord—

5.2.s:
tatkiṃ te tapasaḥ śaktyā brāhmaṇasya vicakṣaṇa.
aparaṃ śṛṇu me vākyaṃ yadbravīmi parisphuṭam.
śṛṇvatāṃ munivṛndānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ dvijottama..6.2.21..
5.2.d:
तत्किं ते तपसः शक्त्या ब्राह्मणस्य विचक्षण.
अपरं शृणु मे वाक्यं यद्ब्रवीमि परिस्फुटम्.
शृण्वतां मुनिवृन्दानां तथान्येषां द्विजोत्तम..6.2.21..
5.2.m: then what is the power of your austerity, O discerning brahmin? / Hear another word of mine which I speak very clearly / while the hosts of sages and others listen, O best of brahmins:

5.2.s:
yadi me na karoṣi tvaṃ vacanaṃ vadato'sakṛt.
tena yajñena yakṣye'haṃ tatkṛtvānyaṃ dvijaṃ gurum..6.2.22..
5.2.d:
यदि मे न करोषि त्वं वचनं वदतोऽसकृत्.
तेन यज्ञेन यक्ष्येऽहं तत्कृत्वान्यं द्विजं गुरुम्..6.2.22..
5.2.m: If you do not do what I repeatedly speak, / I will perform that sacrifice by making another brahmin my guru."

5.2.s:
sūta uvāca.
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vasiṣṭho bhagavāṃstataḥ.
tamuvāca vihasyoccaiḥ kuruṣvaivaṃ mahīpate..6.2.23..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetra māhātmye triśaṃkūpākhyāne triśaṃkuvasiṣṭhasaṃvādavarṇanaṃ nāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ..2..
5.2.d:
सूत उवाच.
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो भगवांस्ततः.
तमुवाच विहस्योच्चैः कुरुष्वैवं महीपते..6.2.23..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्र माहात्म्ये त्रिशंकूपाख्याने त्रिशंकुवसिष्ठसंवादवर्णनं नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः..2..
5.2.m:
Sūta said: / Hearing that speech of his, the venerable Vasiṣṭha then / laughed aloud and said to him: "Do so, O ruler of the earth!"
Thus ends the second chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Dialogue between Triśaṅku and Vasiṣṭha,' in the story of Triśaṅku, in the māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara kṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.3.s:
sūta uvāca.
tataḥ praṇamya bhūyaḥ sa vasiṣṭhaṃ munipuṃgavam.
yayau tatra sutāstasya yatra te śatasaṃkhyakāḥ..6.3.1..
5.3.d:
सूत उवाच.
ततः प्रणम्य भूयः स वसिष्ठं मुनिपुंगवम्.
ययौ तत्र सुतास्तस्य यत्र ते शतसंख्यकाः..6.3.1..
5.3.m: Sūta said: / Then, bowing again to Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of sages, / he went to where his sons, one hundred in number, were.

5.3.s:
tānapi prāha natvā sa tamevārthaṃ narādhipaḥ.
vasiṣṭhavacanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tasya tairapi śaṃsitam..6.3.2..
5.3.d:
तानपि प्राह नत्वा स तमेवार्थं नराधिपः.
वसिष्ठवचनं कृत्स्नं तस्य तैरपि शंसितम्..6.3.2..
5.3.m: Bowing to them as well, the king spoke of that same matter; / the entire speech of Vasiṣṭha was also recounted to him by them.

5.3.s:
tatastānsa punaḥ prāha yuṣmākaṃ janako'dhunā.
aśakto mā divaṃ netuṃ saśarīraṃ visarjitaḥ..6.3.3..
5.3.d:
ततस्तान्स पुनः प्राह युष्माकं जनकोऽधुना.
अशक्तो मा दिवं नेतुं सशरीरं विसर्जितः..6.3.3..
5.3.m: Then he said to them again: "Your father has just now / proven unable to take me to heaven in the body, and has been dismissed.

5.3.s:
tasmādyadi na māṃ yūyaṃ yājayiṣyatha sāṃpratam.
parityajya kariṣyāmi śīghramanyaṃ purohitam..6.3.4..
5.3.d:
तस्माद्यदि न मां यूयं याजयिष्यथ सांप्रतम्.
परित्यज्य करिष्यामि शीघ्रमन्यं पुरोहितम्..6.3.4..
5.3.m: Therefore, if you will not officiate for me now, / I will abandon [you] and quickly appoint another family priest,

5.3.s:
yo māṃ yajñaprabhāvena nayiṣyati surālayam.
anenaiva śarīreṇa sahitaṃ guruputrakāḥ..6.3.5..
5.3.d:
यो मां यज्ञप्रभावेन नयिष्यति सुरालयम्.
अनेनैव शरीरेण सहितं गुरुपुत्रकाः..6.3.5..
5.3.m: who through the power of sacrifice will lead me to the abode of the gods / together with this very body, O sons of the guru!"

5.3.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sarve te munisattamāḥ.
paraṃ kopaṃ samāviṣṭāstamūcuḥ paruṣākṣaraiḥ..6.3.6..
5.3.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते मुनिसत्तमाः.
परं कोपं समाविष्टास्तमूचुः परुषाक्षरैः..6.3.6..
5.3.m: Hearing that speech of his, all those best of sages, / seized by great wrath, addressed him with harsh words:

5.3.s:
yasmāttvayā gurustyakto hitakṛtpāpavānasi.
tasmādbhavādhunā pāpa caṃḍālo lokaniṃditaḥ..6.3.7..
5.3.d:
यस्मात्त्वया गुरुस्त्यक्तो हितकृत्पापवानसि.
तस्माद्भवाधुना पाप चंडालो लोकनिंदितः..6.3.7..
5.3.m: "Because you have abandoned your guru who wished you well, you are sinful. / Therefore become now, O sinner, an outcaste reviled by the world!"

5.3.s:
atha tadvacanāṃte sa tatkṣaṇātpṛthivīpatiḥ.
babhūvāṃtyajarūpāḍhyo vikṛtākāradehabhṛt..6.3.8..
5.3.d:
अथ तद्वचनांते स तत्क्षणात्पृथिवीपतिः.
बभूवांत्यजरूपाढ्यो विकृताकारदेहभृत्..6.3.8..
5.3.m: Then, at the conclusion of their words, that ruler of the earth instantly / took on the form of an outcaste, bearing a deformed body.

5.3.s:
yavamadhyaḥ kṛśagrīvaḥ piṃgākṣo bhugnanāsikaḥ.
kṛṣṇāṃgaḥ śaṃkuvarṇaśca durgaṃdhena samāvṛtaḥ..6.3.9..
5.3.d:
यवमध्यः कृशग्रीवः पिंगाक्षो भुग्ननासिकः.
कृष्णांगः शंकुवर्णश्च दुर्गंधेन समावृतः..6.3.9..
5.3.m: Broad in the middle like a barleycorn, with a withered neck, yellow-brown eyes, and a broken nose, / dark-limbed, peg-colored, and enveloped in a foul stench.

5.3.s:
athātmānaṃ samālokya vikṛtaṃ sa narādhipaḥ.
caṇḍāladharmiṇaṃ sadyo lajjayā'dhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ..6.3.10..
5.3.d:
अथात्मानं समालोक्य विकृतं स नराधिपः.
चण्डालधर्मिणं सद्यो लज्जयाऽधोमुखः स्थितः..6.3.10..
5.3.m: Then, beholding himself deformed, / reduced at once to the state of an outcaste, the king stood with his face cast down in shame.

5.3.s:
yāhiyāhīti vipraistairbhartsyamāno muhurmuhuḥ.
sarvataḥ sārameyaiśca kliśyamāno nirargalaiḥ.
kākakokilasaṃkāśo jīrṇavastrāvaguṃṭhitaḥ..6.3.11..
5.3.d:
याहियाहीति विप्रैस्तैर्भर्त्स्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः.
सर्वतः सारमेयैश्च क्लिश्यमानो निरर्गलैः.
काककोकिलसंकाशो जीर्णवस्त्रावगुंठितः..6.3.11..
5.3.m: Chided repeatedly by those brahmins shouting, "Begone, begone!", / and harassed on all sides by unrestrained dogs, / resembling a crow or a cuckoo, wrapped in tattered rags,

5.3.s:
tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa duḥkhena mahatā vṛtaḥ.
kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ śāṃtirbhaviṣyati..6.3.12..
5.3.d:
ततः स चिन्तयामास दुःखेन महता वृतः.
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि कथं शांतिर्भविष्यति..6.3.12..
5.3.m: he then reflected, overwhelmed with great sorrow: / "What shall I do? Where shall I go? How will peace come to be?

5.3.s:
kiṃ mayaitatsumūrkheṇa vāṃchitaṃ durlabhaṃ padam.
tatprabhāvena vibhraṣṭaḥ kuladharmo'pi me svakaḥ..6.3.13..
5.3.d:
किं मयैतत्सुमूर्खेण वांछितं दुर्लभं पदम्.
तत्प्रभावेन विभ्रष्टः कुलधर्मोऽपि मे स्वकः..6.3.13..
5.3.m: Why did I, a great fool, crave an unattainable station? / Under its influence even my own family duty has perished.

5.3.s:
kiṃ jalaṃ praviśāmyadya kiṃ vā dīptaṃ hutāśanam.
bhakṣayāmi viṣaṃ kiṃ vā kathaṃ syānmṛtyuradya me..6.3.14..
5.3.d:
किं जलं प्रविशाम्यद्य किं वा दीप्तं हुताशनम्.
भक्षयामि विषं किं वा कथं स्यान्मृत्युरद्य मे..6.3.14..
5.3.m: Shall I enter water today, or a blazing fire? / Or shall I consume poison? How may death be mine today?

5.3.s:
anena vapuṣā dārānvīkṣayiṣyāmi tānkatham.
tādṛśena śarīreṇa yābhiḥ saṃkrīḍitaṃ mayā..6.3.15..
5.3.d:
अनेन वपुषा दारान्वीक्षयिष्यामि तान्कथम्.
तादृशेन शरीरेण याभिः संक्रीडितं मया..6.3.15..
5.3.m: How shall I look upon my wives with this form, / with whom I used to sport with such a body?

5.3.s:
kathaṃ putrāṃstathā pautrānsuhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibāṃdhavān.
vīkṣayiṣyāmi tānbhūyastathānyaṃ sevakaṃ janam..6.3.16..
ye mayā nirjitāḥ sarve ripavaḥ saṃgare purā..15..
5.3.d:
कथं पुत्रांस्तथा पौत्रान्सुहृत्संबंधिबांधवान्.
वीक्षयिष्यामि तान्भूयस्तथान्यं सेवकं जनम्..6.3.16..
ये मया निर्जिताः सर्वे रिपवः संगरे पुरा..15..
5.3.m:
How shall I look again upon my sons, grandsons, / friends, relations, and kinsmen, and likewise other servants?
All the enemies whom I conquered in battle of old—

5.3.s: te'dya māmīdṛśaṃ śrutvā harṣaṃ yāsyaṃti nirbhayāḥ..6.3.17..
5.3.d: तेऽद्य मामीदृशं श्रुत्वा हर्षं यास्यंति निर्भयाः..6.3.17..
5.3.m: hearing of me [reduced to] such a state today, they will rejoice, free from fear.

5.3.s:
ye mayā tarpitā dānairbrāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ.
te'dya māmīdṛśaṃ śrutvā saṃbhaviṣyaṃti duḥkhitāḥ..6.3.18..
5.3.d:
ये मया तर्पिता दानैर्ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः.
तेऽद्य मामीदृशं श्रुत्वा संभविष्यंति दुःखिताः..6.3.18..
5.3.m: The brahmins versed in the Vedas whom I satisfied with gifts— / hearing of me [reduced to] such a state today, they will become sorrowful.

5.3.s:
tathā ye suhṛdo'bhīṣṭā nityaṃ mama hite ratāḥ.
kāmavasthāṃ prayāsyanti dṛṣṭvā māṃ sthitamīdṛśam..6.3.19..
5.3.d:
तथा ये सुहृदोऽभीष्टा नित्यं मम हिते रताः.
कामवस्थां प्रयास्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा मां स्थितमीदृशम्..6.3.19..
5.3.m: Likewise, my dear friends who were ever devoted to my welfare— / to what state will they come upon seeing me standing like this?

5.3.s:
bhadrajātyā gajā ye me madāndhāḥ ṣaṣṭihāyanāḥ.
mayā vinā mitho yuddhe kastānadya niyokṣyati..6.3.20..
5.3.d:
भद्रजात्या गजा ये मे मदान्धाः षष्टिहायनाः.
मया विना मिथो युद्धे कस्तानद्य नियोक्ष्यति..6.3.20..
5.3.m: My elephants of noble breed, blinded with rut, sixty years of age— / without me, who will engage them in mutual combat today?

5.3.s:
aśvāstittirakalmāṣāḥ sudāṃtāḥ sādibhirdṛḍhaiḥ.
kastāṃścitrapadanyāsairniyāmyati mayā vinā..6.3.21..
5.3.d:
अश्वास्तित्तिरकल्माषाः सुदांताः सादिभिर्दृढैः.
कस्तांश्चित्रपदन्यासैर्नियाम्यति मया विना..6.3.21..
5.3.m: The horses spotted like partridges, well-broken by sturdy riders— / who will guide them through their intricate paces without me?

5.3.s:
tathā me bhṛtyavargāste kulīnā yuddhadurmadāḥ.
māṃ vinā kasya yāsyaṃti samīpe'dya suduḥkhitāḥ..6.3.22..
5.3.d:
तथा मे भृत्यवर्गास्ते कुलीना युद्धदुर्मदाः.
मां विना कस्य यास्यंति समीपेऽद्य सुदुःखिताः..6.3.22..
5.3.m: Likewise my troops of servants, well-born and furious in battle— / without me, to whom will they go today, deeply afflicted?

5.3.s:
saṃkhyāhīnastathā kośastādṛṅme bahuratnabhāk.
kasya yāsyati saṃbhogaṃ mayā hīnastu rakṣitaḥ..6.3.23..
5.3.d:
संख्याहीनस्तथा कोशस्तादृङ्मे बहुरत्नभाक्.
कस्य यास्यति संभोगं मया हीनस्तु रक्षितः..6.3.23..
5.3.m: And my countless treasury, possessed of many such gems— / for whose enjoyment will it be, bereft of me who protected it?

5.3.s:
tathā me saṃkhyayā hīnaṃ dhānyaṃ gojāvikaṃ mahat.
bhaviṣyati kathaṃ hīnaṃ mayābhīṣṭaistu rakṣitam..6.3.24..
5.3.d:
तथा मे संख्यया हीनं धान्यं गोजाविकं महत्.
भविष्यति कथं हीनं मयाभीष्टैस्तु रक्षितम्..6.3.24..
5.3.m: Likewise my vast store of grain, cattle, goats, and sheep beyond count— / how will it fare, bereft of me though guarded by beloved [servants]?"

5.3.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ rājā sa vilapya ca duḥkhitaḥ.
jagāma nagarābhyāśaṃ padbhyāmeva śanaiḥśanaiḥ..6.3.25..
5.3.d:
एवं बहुविधं राजा स विलप्य च दुःखितः.
जगाम नगराभ्याशं पद्भ्यामेव शनैःशनैः..6.3.25..
5.3.m: Having thus lamented in many ways, the sorrowful king / went slowly on foot toward the vicinity of the city.

5.3.s:
tato rātrau samāsādya svaṃ puraṃ janavarjitam.
dvāre sthitvā samāhūya putraṃ maṃtribhiranvitam..6.3.26..
5.3.d:
ततो रात्रौ समासाद्य स्वं पुरं जनवर्जितम्.
द्वारे स्थित्वा समाहूय पुत्रं मंत्रिभिरन्वितम्..6.3.26..
5.3.m: Then, having reached his city at night when it was deserted by people, / he stood at the gate and summoned his son together with the ministers.

5.3.s:
kathayāmāsa vṛttāṃtaṃ sarvaṃ śāpasamudbhavam.
dūre sthitaḥ sa putrāṇāṃ vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ..6.3.27..
5.3.d:
कथयामास वृत्तांतं सर्वं शापसमुद्भवम्.
दूरे स्थितः स पुत्राणां वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः..6.3.27..
5.3.m: Standing far off, he recounted the whole event born of the curse / of the sons of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

5.3.s:
vajrapātopamaṃ vākyaṃ te'pi tasya niśamya tat.
bāṣpaparyākulairāsyai ruruduḥ śokasaṃyutāḥ..6.3.28..
5.3.d:
वज्रपातोपमं वाक्यं तेऽपि तस्य निशम्य तत्.
बाष्पपर्याकुलैरास्यै रुरुदुः शोकसंयुताः..6.3.28..
5.3.m: Having heard those words of his, which were like a thunderbolt falling, / they too wept, full of sorrow, their faces bathed in tears:

5.3.s:
hā nātha hā mahārāja hā nityaṃ dharmavatsala.
tvayā hīnā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kathamadya suduḥkhitāḥ..6.3.29..
5.3.d:
हा नाथ हा महाराज हा नित्यं धर्मवत्सल.
त्वया हीना भविष्यामः कथमद्य सुदुःखिताः..6.3.29..
5.3.m: “Alas, lord! Alas, great king! Alas, you who are always devoted to righteousness! / Deprived of you, how deeply afflicted shall we become today?

5.3.s:
kimetadyujyate teṣāṃ vāsiṣṭhānāṃ durātmanām.
śāpaṃ daduḥ svayājyasya viśeṣādvinatasya ca..6.3.30..
5.3.d:
किमेतद्युज्यते तेषां वासिष्ठानां दुरात्मनाम्.
शापं ददुः स्वयाज्यस्य विशेषाद्विनतस्य च..6.3.30..
5.3.m: How could this be proper for those wicked sons of Vasiṣṭha? / They pronounced a curse upon their own patron, and one who was especially humble!

5.3.s:
te vayaṃ rājaśārdūla parityajya gṛhādikam.
antyajatvaṃ gamiṣyāmastvayā sārdhamasaṃśayam..6.3.31..
5.3.d:
ते वयं राजशार्दूल परित्यज्य गृहादिकम्.
अन्त्यजत्वं गमिष्यामस्त्वया सार्धमसंशयम्..6.3.31..
5.3.m: We, O tiger among kings, having abandoned home and all else, / shall undoubtedly go into the status of outcastes together with you!”

5.3.s:
triśaṃkuruvāca.
bhaktiścedasti yuṣmākaṃ mamopari nirargala.
tanme putrasya maṃtritvaṃ sarve kuruta sāṃpratam..6.3.32..
5.3.d:
त्रिशंकुरुवाच.
भक्तिश्चेदस्ति युष्माकं ममोपरि निरर्गल.
तन्मे पुत्रस्य मंत्रित्वं सर्वे कुरुत सांप्रतम्..6.3.32..
5.3.m: Triśaṅku said: / “If you have unhindered devotion toward me, / then all of you serve as ministers to my son right now.

5.3.s:
hariścaṃdraḥ suputroyaṃ mama jyeṣṭhaḥ suvallabhaḥ.
niyojayadhvamavyagrāḥ padavyāṃ mama satvaram..6.3.33..
5.3.d:
हरिश्चंद्रः सुपुत्रोयं मम ज्येष्ठः सुवल्लभः.
नियोजयध्वमव्यग्राः पदव्यां मम सत्वरम्..6.3.33..
5.3.m: Hariścandra, this good son of mine, is my eldest and very dear to me. / Free from anxiety, quickly install him in my place.

5.3.s:
ahaṃ punaḥ kariṣyāmi yanme manasi saṃsthitam.
mṛtyuṃ vā saṃprayāsyāmi sadeho vā surālayam..6.3.34..
5.3.d:
अहं पुनः करिष्यामि यन्मे मनसि संस्थितम्.
मृत्युं वा संप्रयास्यामि सदेहो वा सुरालयम्..6.3.34..
5.3.m: As for me, I shall do what rests in my mind: / I shall either meet death, or go in this very body to the abode of the gods.”

5.3.s:
evamuktvā parityajya sarvāṃstānsa mahīpatiḥ.
jagāmāraṇyamāśritya padbhyāmeva śanaiḥ śanaiḥ..6.3.35..
5.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा परित्यज्य सर्वांस्तान्स महीपतिः.
जगामारण्यमाश्रित्य पद्भ्यामेव शनैः शनैः..6.3.35..
5.3.m: Having spoken thus, having abandoned them all, the king / set out on foot, slowly, taking refuge in the forest.

5.3.s:
tepi sanmaṃtriṇastūrṇaṃ putraṃ tasya susammatam.
rājye niyojayāsamāsurnādavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ..6.3.36..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye triśaṃkūpākhyāne hariścandrarājyopalaṃbhonāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ..3..
5.3.d:
तेपि सन्मंत्रिणस्तूर्णं पुत्रं तस्य सुसम्मतम्.
राज्ये नियोजयासमासुर्नादवादित्रनिःस्वनैः..6.3.36..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये त्रिशंकूपाख्याने हरिश्चन्द्रराज्योपलंभोनाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः..3..
5.3.m:
Those good ministers, too, quickly installed his well-esteemed son / on the throne, amidst the sounds of noisy musical instruments.
Thus ends the third chapter, named ‘Obtaining of the Kingdom by Hariścandra’ in the story of Triśaṅku, in the glorification of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.4.s:
sūta uvāca.
triśaṃkuriti saṃcintya viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim.
manasā suciraṃ kālaṃ tataścakre viniścayam..6.4.1..
5.4.d:
सूत उवाच.
त्रिशंकुरिति संचिन्त्य विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम्.
मनसा सुचिरं कालं ततश्चक्रे विनिश्चयम्..6.4.1..
5.4.m: Sūta said: / Having pondered thus, Triśaṅku, after a long time, / made a firm resolve in his mind regarding the great sage Viśvāmitra:

5.4.s:
viśvāmitraṃ parityajya nānyosti bhuvanatraye.
yaḥ kuryānme paritrāṇaṃ duḥkhādasmātsudāruṇāt..6.4.2..
5.4.d:
विश्वामित्रं परित्यज्य नान्योस्ति भुवनत्रये.
यः कुर्यान्मे परित्राणं दुःखादस्मात्सुदारुणात्..6.4.2..
5.4.m: “Apart from Viśvāmitra, there is no one else in the three worlds / who can deliver me from this terrible suffering.”

5.4.s:
kurukṣetraṃ samuddiśya pratasthe sa tataḥ param.
suśrāṃtaḥ kṣutpipāsārto mārgapṛcchāparāyaṇaḥ..6.4.3..
5.4.d:
कुरुक्षेत्रं समुद्दिश्य प्रतस्थे स ततः परम्.
सुश्रांतः क्षुत्पिपासार्तो मार्गपृच्छापरायणः..6.4.3..
5.4.m: Setting Kurukṣetra as his destination, he then set out, / utterly exhausted, afflicted by hunger and thirst, constantly inquiring about the way.

5.4.s:
tataḥ kālena saṃprāpya kurukṣetraṃ sa pārthivaḥ.
yatnenānveṣayāmāsa viśvāmitrāśramaṃ tataḥ..6.4.4..
5.4.d:
ततः कालेन संप्राप्य कुरुक्षेत्रं स पार्थिवः.
यत्नेनान्वेषयामास विश्वामित्राश्रमं ततः..6.4.4..
5.4.m: Then, having reached Kurukṣetra in the course of time, the king / eagerly searched for the hermitage of Viśvāmitra.

5.4.s:
evaṃ cānveṣamāṇena tena bhūmibhṛtā tadā.
sudūrādeva saṃdṛṣṭaṃ nīladrumakadambakam..6.4.5..
5.4.d:
एवं चान्वेषमाणेन तेन भूमिभृता तदा.
सुदूरादेव संदृष्टं नीलद्रुमकदम्बकम्..6.4.5..
5.4.m: And while the king was searching thus, / he saw from afar a cluster of dark trees,

5.4.s:
upariṣṭādbakairhaṃsairbhramamāṇaiḥ samaṃtataḥ.
āṭibhirmadgubhiścaiva samantājjalapakṣibhiḥ..6.4.6..
5.4.d:
उपरिष्टाद्बकैर्हंसैर्भ्रममाणैः समंततः.
आटिभिर्मद्गुभिश्चैव समन्ताज्जलपक्षिभिः..6.4.6..
5.4.m: with cranes and swans wandering all around overhead, / along with waterfowl, diver-birds, and water-birds on every side.

5.4.s:
sa matvā salilaṃ tatra pipāsārto mahīpatiḥ.
pratasthe satvaro hṛṣṭo jalavātahṛtaklamaḥ..6.4.7..
5.4.d:
स मत्वा सलिलं तत्र पिपासार्तो महीपतिः.
प्रतस्थे सत्वरो हृष्टो जलवातहृतक्लमः..6.4.7..
5.4.m: Thinking there was water there, the king, tormented by thirst, / set off quickly, delighted, his fatigue removed by the breeze over the water.

5.4.s:
athāpaśyanmanohāri saumyasattvaniṣevitam.
āśramaṃ naditīrasthaṃ manaḥśokavināśanam..6.4.8..
5.4.d:
अथापश्यन्मनोहारि सौम्यसत्त्वनिषेवितम्.
आश्रमं नदितीरस्थं मनःशोकविनाशनम्..6.4.8..
5.4.m: Then he saw a captivating hermitage, frequented by gentle creatures, / situated on the bank of a river, dispelling the sorrow of the mind,

5.4.s:
puṣpitaiḥ phalitairvṛkṣaiḥ samaṃtātparivāritam.
vividhairmadhurārāvairnāditaṃ vihagottamaiḥ..6.4.9..
5.4.d:
पुष्पितैः फलितैर्वृक्षैः समंतात्परिवारितम्.
विविधैर्मधुरारावैर्नादितं विहगोत्तमैः..6.4.9..
5.4.m: surrounded on all sides by trees bearing flowers and fruits, / resounding with the sweet calls of various excellent birds,

5.4.s:
krīḍaṃti nakulāḥ sarpairūlūkā yatra vāyasaiḥ.
